The Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) has released the eligible and not eligible candidate list for the post of Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer / Deputy Director (Group-A), advertised under Advt No. 004/2026. This list is a crucial update for every candidate who applied online between 20 March 2026 and 9 April 2026, as it confirms whether their application has cleared the scrutiny stage and whether they will move ahead in the recruitment process. Candidates can check their status directly by downloading the official PDFs and matching their application/roll number.

Click Here: MPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer / Deputy Director Not Eligible Candidate List

MPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer Result 2026 - Quick Overview

This section gives a snapshot of the recruitment so candidates immediately understand which post, advertisement, and stage this result belongs to before going through the detailed breakdown below.

Particulars Details
Recruiting Body Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC)
Post Name Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer / Deputy Director
Group Group-A
Advertisement Number 004/2026
Total Vacancies 21 Posts
Application Period 20 March 2026 - 9 April 2026
Current Update Eligible & Not Eligible Candidate List released
Job Location Maharashtra
Official Website mpsc.gov.in

What Is the MPSC Eligible Candidate List?

The eligible candidate list is the official record published by MPSC confirming which applicants have successfully passed the initial document and application scrutiny stage for the Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer / Deputy Director post. Only candidates featured on this list are permitted to proceed to the next stage of selection, such as the screening test or interview.

  • It includes candidates whose application form, category claim, age, and eligibility documents (such as ex-servicemen rank certificate and Marathi language proficiency proof) matched MPSC's prescribed criteria.
  • Being on this list does not guarantee final selection it only confirms eligibility to continue in the recruitment process.
  • Candidates must verify their name/roll number directly from the official PDF linked by MPSC, as no third-party source can confirm individual status.

What Is the MPSC Not Eligible Candidate List?

The not eligible candidate list contains applicants whose forms were rejected during scrutiny, along with the post-wise and category-wise reason for rejection. This section helps such candidates understand why they were excluded and whether they have any recourse.

  • Common reasons for rejection in this category of recruitment typically include incomplete documents, rank/service certificate not matching the required Major-and-above criterion, missing Marathi language proof, or age/category mismatch.
  • MPSC generally provides a specific remark against each rejected application explaining the exact reason.
  • Candidates who believe their rejection is incorrect should check the official notification for any objection or grievance window provided by MPSC, since timelines for raising objections are usually short.

How to Download the MPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer Candidate List PDF

This section explains the simplest way to access and check your name in the official lists without confusion.

  1. Visit the official MPSC website: mpsc.gov.in
  2. Go to the "Recruitment" or "Advertisement" section and locate Advt No. 004/2026.
  3. Click on the relevant link for Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer / Deputy Director result updates.
  4. Open the Eligible Candidate List or Not Eligible Candidate List PDF.
  5. Use Ctrl+F (Find) to search your roll number, application ID, or name.
  6. Download and save the PDF for future reference.

About the MPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer / Deputy Director Post

Before checking the result, it helps to understand the post itself its eligibility, age limit, and pay scale since this context explains why MPSC's scrutiny stage is particularly strict for this role.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Candidates must have ceased to be a serving member of the Armed Forces of the Union and must have held the rank of Major and above in the Army, or an equivalent rank in the Navy or Air Force.
  • Candidates must possess adequate knowledge of Marathi, sufficient to speak, read, and write the language with facility.
  • If officers of the requisite rank are unavailable, those holding the rank of Lieutenant and above (or equivalent) may also be considered.

Age Limit

The maximum age limit for the Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer / Deputy Director post is 55 years for all categories, as specified in the official advertisement.

Salary / Pay Scale

Selected candidates for this Group-A post will receive a pay scale of approximately ₹67,700 to ₹2,08,700, along with applicable government allowances, as per Maharashtra Government service rules.

MPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer Selection Process 2026

Understanding the stages ahead helps eligible candidates prepare for what comes next after this scrutiny result.

Stage Description
Application Scrutiny Verification of documents, rank certificate, and category claims (current stage)
Screening/Written Test Conducted if the number of eligible applicants is large
Interview Personal interview to assess suitability for the post
Final Merit List Prepared based on interview marks (or combined screening + interview marks)

What Should Candidates in the Not Eligible List Do Next?

Candidates appearing in the not eligible list should not assume the process is over without first checking the specific remark mentioned against their name in the PDF. If the rejection appears to be a documentation error, candidates can refer to the official notification on mpsc.gov.in for any objection window and the prescribed procedure to raise a grievance, since MPSC may allow limited corrections in certain cases.

Important Dates for MPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer Recruitment 2026

Event Date
Online Application Start Date 20 March 2026
Online Application Last Date 9 April 2026
Eligible/Not Eligible Candidate List Released 24 June 2026

Ordnance Factory Itarsi CPW Merit List 2026 - 828 Candidates Shortlisted for Trade Test

Ordnance Factory Itarsi (OFI), functioning under Munitions India Limited (MIL) and the Ministry of Defence, has released its Tenure Based CPW (Chemical Process Worker) shortlist for 2026. A total of 828 provisionally eligible candidates have been called for the Trade Test / Practical Test, scheduled from 6 July to 11 July 2026, with reporting time fixed at 8:30 AM each day. Call letters have already been emailed to shortlisted candidates, and the schedule has been organised strictly by roll number.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

This article explains everything candidates need to know the shortlist status, exam-wise roll number schedule, exam venue and directions, the document checklist, and what to do if you haven't received your call letter by email.

Click Here: Ordnance Factory Itarsi CPW Merit List 2026

What Is the Ordnance Factory Itarsi CPW Merit List 2026?

This section clarifies exactly what stage of the selection process this list represents, since many candidates confuse a "shortlist for testing" with a "final selection list."

The list released on 22 June 2026 is not the final selection merit list. It is the list of 828 provisionally eligible candidates who have cleared the NAC (National Apprenticeship Certificate)-based cut-off and have therefore been shortlisted to appear for the Trade Test / Practical Test. The final merit list for actual engagement will be prepared only after this Trade Test is conducted, combined with candidates' NAC marks, followed by document verification.

Detail Information
Organisation Ordnance Factory Itarsi (Munitions India Limited)
Post Tenure Based CPW (Chemical Process Worker)
Stage Shortlist for Trade Test / Practical Test
Candidates Shortlisted 828
Reference Number CBC 10201/12/0094/2526 (EN 61/72)
Notice Date 22 June 2026
Test Dates 6 July - 11 July 2026
Reporting Time 8:30 AM
Test Start Time 9:00 AM
Test Venue Ayudh Nirmani Higher Secondary School, Ordnance Factory Estate, Itarsi

Ordnance Factory Itarsi Trade Test Schedule 2026 (Roll Number-Wise)

This section gives the exact date-wise breakup of roll numbers so candidates can immediately check which day they are required to report for the test.

The Trade Test / Practical Test will run across six days, from Monday, 6 July, to Saturday, 11 July 2026. Each day covers a specific block of roll numbers, so candidates should match their own roll number against the table below to confirm their reporting date.

Date Day Roll Number Range
6 July 2026 Monday 4001 - 4144
7 July 2026 Tuesday 4145 - 4300
8 July 2026 Wednesday 4301 - 4450
9 July 2026 Thursday 4451 - 4600
10 July 2026 Friday 4601 - 4750
11 July 2026 Saturday 4751 - 4828

Reporting Time, Test Timing and Venue Details

This section covers when and where candidates must report, plus how to reach the venue if travelling from outside Itarsi.

Candidates must arrive well before the test begins, since late entry is not guaranteed. The test will be conducted at a single designated venue within the Ordnance Factory Estate.

  • Reporting Time: 8:30 AM (mandatory arrival deadline)
  • Test Start Time: 9:00 AM
  • Venue: Ayudh Nirmani Higher Secondary School, Ordnance Factory Estate, Itarsi
  • Distance from Itarsi Railway Station: Approximately 16 km, located on NH-69 (Betul-Nagpur Highway)
  • Local Transport: A paid bus service runs between Itarsi Bus Stand and the OFI Estate from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM

What If You Haven't Received the Call Letter by Email?

This section addresses a common concern among shortlisted candidates who are unsure whether they can still attend the test without an emailed admit card.

Candidates who do not find a call letter or admit card in their email inbox can still appear for the Trade Test. They simply need to verify that their own name and father's name appear in the official shortlisted candidates' list, and then report on the scheduled date by following the standard reporting instructions.

Important: If a candidate's name appears on the list but they remain absent because they did not receive the email, Ordnance Factory Itarsi will not be held responsible. Every shortlisted candidate is strongly advised to personally check their name in the list rather than waiting for an email confirmation.

Documents Required on the Day of the Trade Test

This section lists the mandatory documents candidates must carry, since incomplete documentation can affect participation in the test.

Candidates must carry both identity proof and the original documents submitted earlier with their application. The following checklist applies to every shortlisted candidate:

  • Aadhaar Card (original, with a clearly visible photograph)
  • If Aadhaar is unavailable, any one of the following in original: Voter ID, Driving License, PAN Card, or Passport
  • Original copies of all documents whose photocopies were submitted along with the application form
  • A recent passport-size photograph

Items Strictly Prohibited at the Test Venue

  • Mobile phones
  • Any other electronic gadgets or devices
  • Note: No boarding or lodging facility is available at or near the OFI Estate, so candidates travelling from outside Itarsi should plan same-day travel accordingly.

Important Points Candidates Must Know Before the Test

This section highlights critical conditions that affect a candidate's eligibility and participation, and should be read carefully before the test date.

  • Appearing for the test does not guarantee a job offer. Participation in the Trade Test/Practical Test does not automatically make a candidate eligible for engagement. Final appointment depends on the merit list, available vacancies, fulfilment of all eligibility criteria, character verification, medical examination, and document verification.
  • Call letters were issued based on the NAC cut-off. For each feeder trade, a cut-off percentage based on National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) marks was applied. Only candidates meeting or exceeding this cut-off received the email call letter.
  • No requests for change of date or venue will be entertained. Candidates who fail to report at the specified venue on their allotted date risk having their candidature cancelled without further notice.
  • Check the official websites before travelling. Candidates should verify the latest Trade Test date and time on the MIL website (munitionsindia.in) and the DDPDOO website (ddpdoo.gov.in) before starting their journey, in case of any last-minute change.

Background: Ordnance Factory Itarsi CPW Recruitment 2026

This section gives quick context on the recruitment drive this shortlist belongs to, useful for candidates who are new to this notification.

Ordnance Factory Itarsi had earlier released its Tenure Based CPW recruitment notification for 265 vacancies under the primary trade of AOCP (Attendant Operator Chemical Plant) and other specified feeder trades such as Fitter, Electrician, Machinist, and Turner. As per the official selection process, candidates are first shortlisted on the basis of their NAC marks against a trade-specific cut-off, then called for the Trade Test/Practical Test, after which a final merit list is prepared by combining both sets of marks before document verification and engagement.

Heavy Vehicles Factory (HVF), Avadi, a unit of Armoured Vehicles Nigam Limited (AVNL), has released the shortlist of candidates for Document Verification (DV) and Trade Test for engagement as Junior Technician (Contract) on Fixed Term Employment. This list, issued against Advertisement No. HVF/RG/FTB/RECT/JTC/2026/01 dated 25 January 2026, includes the names of 227 shortlisted candidates across six trades, along with their Trade Test dates, venue, and the complete list of documents required at the time of verification.

Click Here: HVF Avadi Junior Technician Result 2026

What Is This HVF Avadi Notice About?

This section explains the purpose and nature of the document so candidates understand exactly what has been released and what it means for their application.

HVF Avadi has notified that the candidates listed in the official PDF have been shortlisted purely for Document Verification and Trade Test this is not a final selection or merit list. Being called for DV and Trade Test does not guarantee final engagement as Junior Technician. The factory has clearly stated that the Trade Test will be conducted only in the trade for which a candidate has been called, and clearing the test is one step in a multi-stage selection process, not the final outcome.

HVF Avadi Junior Technician DV & Trade Test Schedule

This section covers the exact dates on which candidates in each trade must report for their Trade Test, along with the common venue and reporting details.

The Trade Test for all six trades is spread across three consecutive days 26, 27, and 28 June 2026 at a single venue.

Trade Trade Test Date Venue
HTO 26 June 2026 HVF Training School, Avadi
FAE 26 June 2026 HVF Training School, Avadi
SS&B 26 June 2026 HVF Training School, Avadi
Machinist 26, 27 & 28 June 2026 HVF Training School, Avadi
OMHE 27 June 2026 HVF Training School, Avadi
Rigger 28 June 2026 HVF Training School, Avadi

Since the Machinist trade has the largest number of candidates, it has been split across all three days. Candidates should check their specific name and assigned date carefully in the official shortlist rather than assuming a single common date.

Trade-Wise Breakdown of Shortlisted Candidates

This section gives a quick overview of how many candidates have been shortlisted in each trade, helping applicants understand the scale of competition and category-wise distribution.

A total of 227 candidates have been shortlisted across the following trades:

  • Machinist - the largest group, shortlisted across all three test dates (26, 27, and 28 June 2026)
  • HTO (Heavy Transport Operator) - shortlisted for 26 June 2026
  • FAE - shortlisted for 26 June 2026
  • SS&B - shortlisted for 26 June 2026
  • OMHE (Operator Material Handling Equipment) - shortlisted for 27 June 2026
  • Rigger - shortlisted for 28 June 2026

Candidates' date of birth has also been mentioned alongside each name in the official list, which can help in cases of similar or duplicate names appearing in the same trade.

How to Check Your Name in the HVF Avadi Shortlist

This section explains the simplest way for candidates to confirm whether they have been shortlisted and what details to verify once they find their name.

To check your status, candidates should:

  1. Open the official shortlist PDF released by HVF Avadi.
  2. Search for their name and date of birth, since some names are repeated across the list.
  3. Note the trade mentioned against their name the Trade Test will be conducted only for that specific trade.
  4. Note the exact Trade Test date assigned, as it varies by trade (and by sub-batch for Machinist).
  5. Confirm the reporting venue, which is the same for all trades: HVF Training School, Avadi.

Documents Required for Document Verification

This section lists all original certificates and documents that shortlisted candidates must carry, along with one self-attested photocopy set, on their reporting day.

Candidates must bring the following original documents along with one set of self-attested photocopies. Candidates who fail to produce the relevant certificates will not be allowed to appear for the Trade Test.

  • SSLC / Matric / 10th Certificate
  • National Trade Certificate (NTC) Mark Sheet and NTC issued by NCVT for the relevant trade
  • National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) Mark Sheet and NAC issued by NCVT for the relevant trade
  • Valid Community Certificate (OBC/SC) in the prescribed format for Central Government jobs
  • EWS Certificate valid for the year 2024-25
  • Discharge Certificate (for Ex-Servicemen candidates)
  • Disability Certificate (for Persons with Benchmark Disability)
  • Experience Certificate, if applicable, for the relevant trade
  • Aadhaar Card
  • PAN Card
  • Driving License for Heavy Vehicles (wherever applicable)
  • Police Verification Report
  • Medical Test report (as per Annexure-5)

Important Points Candidates Should Know

This section highlights the key conditions mentioned in the official notice that every shortlisted candidate must be aware of before the verification day.

  • Document Verification and Trade Test are mandatory steps; missing required documents means the candidate will not be permitted to take the Trade Test.
  • The Trade Test will be conducted strictly for the trade against the candidate's name not for any other trade.
  • Being shortlisted and appearing for the Trade Test does not guarantee final engagement as Junior Technician (Contract).
  • The notice has been issued by N.N. Narendra, General Manager/HR (Cent)-II, for CGM/HVF, Heavy Vehicles Factory, a Unit of AVNL.

This article explains how to download the result, what it contains, and what comes next in the selection process.

JKSSB Field Assistant Result 2026 - Overview

This section gives a quick snapshot of the result so candidates can understand the key facts before going into details.

The JKSSB has issued the result/scoresheet for the Field Assistant post on its official website, jkssb.nic.in. This recruitment falls under Advertisement Notification No. 03 of 2021, and the written examination was conducted in OMR mode for the Forest, Ecology and Environment Department.

JKSSB Field Assistant Result 2026 - Direct Download Link

This section provides the exact link candidates need to access their result PDF.

Candidates can access the official result PDF directly from the JKSSB website using the link below.

Direct Link: JKSSB Field Assistant Result 2026 PDF

Since the document opens directly from the JKSSB server, candidates should keep a stable internet connection while downloading, as result PDFs on the official portal can take longer to load due to heavy traffic.

How to Check JKSSB Field Assistant Result 2026

This section explains the step-by-step method to view and download the result.

Candidates can follow these simple steps to check their result on the official JKSSB website:

  1. Visit the official JKSSB website at jkssb.nic.in.
  2. Go to the "What's New" section on the homepage.
  3. Look for the notification titled "Result/Scoresheet of Written Test for the post of Field Assistant".
  4. Click on the relevant PDF link.
  5. The result will open as a PDF document on the screen.
  6. Use the Ctrl+F shortcut to search for your roll number quickly within the document.
  7. Download and save the PDF for future reference.

Background of the JKSSB Field Assistant Recruitment

This section explains the recruitment process leading up to the result, helping candidates understand the full timeline.

The Field Assistant post falls under the Forest, Ecology and Environment Department and was advertised under Notification No. 03 of 2021. The recruitment process for the 2026 cycle followed this sequence:

  • Written Examination: JKSSB conducted the OMR-based written test for Field Assistant on 20 May 2026.
  • Provisional Answer Key: The board released the provisional answer key shortly after the exam, allowing candidates to raise objections within a stipulated window using documentary proof.
  • Final Answer Key & Result: Following the objection period, JKSSB reviewed representations before finalizing the answer key and proceeding to result declaration.

This is consistent with the standard JKSSB recruitment pattern, where the result/scoresheet is published only after the provisional answer key objections are resolved.

What Information Does the Result PDF Contain?

This section explains the typical details found in a JKSSB scoresheet, based on the board's standard result format for other recent posts.

JKSSB result/scoresheet documents for written examinations generally include:

  • Roll number of the candidate
  • Marks obtained in the written examination
  • Category of the candidate
  • Post and advertisement notification details
  • Instructions regarding the next stage of selection (such as document verification)

Candidates should open the PDF and verify these details carefully against their own application and admit card records.

Selection Process After the Result

This section outlines what typically follows once the written test result is announced for JKSSB posts under this recruitment category.

After the declaration of the written test result, the JKSSB recruitment process for Field Assistant generally moves forward as follows:

  • Candidates whose names/roll numbers appear in the qualifying range are shortlisted for Document Verification.
  • JKSSB separately issues notices specifying the schedule, venue, and list of documents required for verification.
  • Once document verification is complete, the board prepares and releases the Final Selection List for the post.

Candidates are advised to keep checking the official JKSSB website regularly, since notices for document verification are usually published as a separate notification after the result.

Important Points to Verify in the Result

This section lists the key checks candidates must make immediately after downloading the result.

After downloading the result PDF, candidates should verify the following details carefully:

  • Correct spelling of name and roll number
  • Category mentioned (General/Reserved)
  • Marks obtained in the written test
  • Any discrepancy in personal details

If any error is found, candidates should contact JKSSB through the official communication channels mentioned on the website without delay.

Click Here: GSSSB Junior Scientific Assistant Final Result 2026

Why Was the GSSSB Junior Scientific Assistant Result Revised?

This section explains the reason behind GSSSB cancelling its 20 June 2026 result and issuing a fresh one on 23 June 2026.

After the original final result was declared on 20 June 2026, GSSSB received representations from candidates regarding the outcome. Following an internal re-verification at the Board level, GSSSB found that corrections were required in the selection and waiting lists. As a result, the Board has officially declared the 20 June 2026 result and its accompanying notice as null and void, replacing it with the revised lists detailed in this notification.

GSSSB Junior Scientific Assistant Recruitment: Key Details

This section gives a quick overview of the recruitment, exam, and notification details relevant to this result.

Particular Details
Recruiting Body Gujarat Subordinate Services Selection Board (GSSSB)
Post Name Junior Scientific Assistant, Class-3
Advertisement Number 317/2024-25
Department Narmada, Water Resources, Water Supply and Kalpasar Department
Office Gujarat Engineering Research Institute (GERI), Vadodara
Total Posts 40
Exam Pattern MCQ-CBRT (Computer Based Recruitment Test)
Candidates Appeared in Exam 716
Document Verification List Dates 22-01-2026, 26-02-2026, 16-06-2026, 18-06-2026
Original Final Result Date 20-06-2026 (Cancelled)

GSSSB Junior Scientific Assistant Revised Result: What's Included

This section explains the three annexures released as part of the revised result and what each one contains.

GSSSB has released the revised outcome in three separate annexures, each covering a different category of candidates:

  • Annexure-A - Revised Selection List: Contains the final list of 40 candidates recommended for appointment, selected on the basis of merit, minimum qualifying marks, and category-wise vacancy distribution after document verification.
  • Annexure-B - Revised Waiting List: Contains 9 candidates placed on the waiting list, determined using the same merit and category-wise criteria.

How to Check Your Name in CSU Non-Teaching Eligibility List 2026

Key Instructions for Provisionally Eligible Candidates

The official notification contains several critical instructions that every eligible candidate must read carefully before appearing in the written examination. Ignoring these conditions may result in cancellation of candidature.

1. Provisional Nature of Eligibility

The eligibility granted is purely provisional and based on the candidate's self-certification. It is entirely the candidate's responsibility to ensure they meet all qualification and eligibility criteria specified for the applied post. Being on the list does not guarantee appointment or progression to further stages of recruitment.

2. Admit Card Issuance

Admit cards for the written examination will be issued provisionally. The admit card will indicate the examination center details including venue and address. Candidates must note that the mere issuance of an admit card does not confer any right to claim appointment.

3. Examination City is Final

The city selected by the candidate during the online application process will be treated as the final examination center city. The examination center will be allotted within that city only. No request for change of examination city will be entertained under any circumstances. Candidates are advised to plan their travel and accommodation in advance.

4. Document Verification Before Skill Test or Interview

Shortlisting for the Skill Test or Interview will be subject to verification of all original documents, certificates, and claims by the competent authority. Eligibility for the written examination does not automatically guarantee qualification for subsequent recruitment stages.

5. Rejection of Applications

Applications that were not duly filled, were incomplete, or for which the fee was not paid have been technically rejected. The university will not entertain any communication or representation regarding such rejected applications.

6. Cancellation of Candidature

A candidate's candidature is liable to be rejected or cancelled at any stage - including after declaration of results - if they are found ineligible as of the cut-off date, or if any information furnished in the application is found to be false, incorrect, misleading, or based on forged/fabricated documents. Appropriate action under applicable rules may also be initiated in such cases.

This section explains the purpose of a waiting list and why SBI releases one after the final result. In short, the waiting list lets SBI fill leftover vacancies without conducting a fresh recruitment cycle.

After SBI declares the final SBI Clerk merit list, some selected candidates do not join, or they resign shortly after joining. To fill these resulting vacancies, SBI maintains a waiting list of candidates who narrowly missed the final cut-off. The 1st Waiting List released on 19th June 2026 is the first such list prepared for this purpose, and it contains the roll numbers of candidates now provisionally selected against these vacant posts.

Why Did SBI Release a Waiting List?

This section explains the reason behind the waiting list, addressing why some candidates are getting a second chance even after the final result was declared.

A waiting list is generated to fill vacancies left vacant due to two main reasons:

  • Non-joining: Some originally selected candidates choose not to join SBI after final selection.
  • Resignation: Some candidates join but resign shortly afterward, freeing up their position.

Rather than running an entirely new selection process, SBI fills these vacancies from the existing pool of candidates who appeared in the merit list but missed selection by a narrow margin.

What Is the HPRCA Teacher Admit Card 2026?

This section explains what the HPRCA Teacher Admit Card actually is and why it matters before exam day.

The HPRCA Teacher Admit Card 2026, also called the hall ticket or roll number slip, is the mandatory entry document issued by the Himachal Pradesh Rajya Chayan Aayog (HPRCA), Hamirpur for candidates appearing in the Computer Based Test (CBT) / OMR-based screening test for various Teacher posts. No candidate is permitted inside the examination centre without this document. HPRCA is currently conducting recruitment for 894 Teacher posts under Advertisement No. 09/2026 (dated 16 April 2026), covering eight subjects in CBSE-affiliated Government Schools across Himachal Pradesh:

HPRCA Public Administration Teacher 2026 - Post Details

This section explains who can apply for the Public Administration Teacher post and what the eligibility requirements are, since admit card eligibility checks are tied to these criteria.

Eligibility Criteria for Teacher (Public Administration)

To be eligible for Post Code 26034, candidates must meet:

  • A Master's Degree in Public Administration from a recognized university with a minimum of 50% marks in aggregate
  • A Bachelor of Education (B.Ed.) with minimum 50% marks
  • A passed Teacher Eligibility Test (TET), conducted by the H.P. Board of School Education, Dharamshala, or another government-authorized agency
  • Proficiency in teaching both Hindi and English
  • HP-domiciled SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates get a 5% relaxation in the minimum qualifying marks
  • Age between 18- 45 years as on 1 January 2026

Engagement Terms

Selected Public Administration Teachers will receive a fixed honorarium of ₹30,000 per month, paid for 10 months in an academic year, under a 5-year scheme-based engagement. This is a contractual position it does not count as regular government service, and benefits like pension, DA, HRA, or TA do not apply.

HPRCA Teacher Exam Date 2026 - Current Status

This section explains what has been officially confirmed about exam scheduling so far, since admit card release always follows the exam date announcement.

As of the latest available HPRCA press note (23 June 2026), the commission has confirmed CBT dates for four subjects only:

Teacher (Sociology) 26029 14/15 July 2026

No CBT date has been officially announced yet for Teacher (Public Administration), Post Code 26034, based on currently available HPRCA notices. Candidates for this post should continue checking the official website, as HPRCA has been releasing exam dates and admit cards for different subjects in separate phases throughout 2026.

How to Download HPRCA Teacher Admit Card 2026 (Step-by-Step)

This section explains the exact process HPRCA uses to release admit cards, based on its established pattern for other Teacher posts under this same recruitment drive.

Once the admit card link for your post goes live, follow these steps:

  1. Visit the official website: hprca.hp.gov.in
  2. Go to the homepage notice/press note section and locate the "Admit Card" link for your specific post (e.g., Public Administration Teacher)
  3. Log in using your Application ID / Registration Number and password (or date of birth, where applicable)
  4. Click on the Admit Card / Roll Number Slip option
  5. Your HPRCA Teacher Admit Card 2026 will display on screen verify all details carefully
  6. Download the admit card and take a clear printout
  7. Note your roll number and exam centre details, which are also sent via SMS to your registered mobile number

What Details Are Printed on the HPRCA Teacher Admit Card?

This section explains what information candidates should check carefully right after downloading their admit card.

The HPRCA Teacher Admit Card 2026 typically includes:

  • Candidate's name, photograph, and signature
  • Roll number and Application ID
  • Post applied for and post code
  • Exam date, shift timing, and reporting time
  • Complete exam centre name and address
  • Candidate's category and any applicable sub-category
  • General instructions for exam day conduct

Candidates must verify every detail immediately after downloading and report any discrepancy to HPRCA right away.

Documents to Carry to the Examination Centre

This section lists what candidates must bring along with the admit card to avoid being denied entry.

  • A printed copy of the HPRCA Teacher Admit Card
  • One original valid photo ID proof Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, PAN Card, or Driving Licence
  • Note: Electronic devices, including mobile phones, are strictly prohibited inside the examination hall

HPRCA Teacher Selection Process 2026

This section explains what happens after the CBT, so candidates know what to expect once the admit card stage is over.

The selection process for all HPRCA Teacher posts, including Public Administration, follows these stages:

  1. Computer Based Test (CBT) / OMR Screening Test 120 marks, objective MCQs, 90 minutes duration. No personal interview is conducted.
  2. Qualifying Marks Minimum 45% for General category and 40% for SC/ST/OBC/WFB categories (subject to relaxation if insufficient candidates qualify).
  3. Normalization If the CBT is held across multiple shifts, scores are normalized using the Z-Score (Mean and Standard Deviation) method.
  4. Merit List & Waiting Panel A category-wise merit list is prepared based on CBT marks; ties are resolved using marks in the essential qualification, then age (senior preferred), then alphabetically.
  5. Document Verification Shortlisted candidates must produce original certificates and self-attested photocopies for verification.

What to Do If the Admit Card Link Doesn't Work

This section covers common troubleshooting steps for candidates unable to access their admit card.

  • Double-check that you are using the correct Application ID and password used during registration
  • Clear your browser cache or try a different browser if the page doesn't load
  • Confirm that the admit card for your specific post and post code has actually been released HPRCA activates links post-wise, not all at once
  • If your roll number or details appear incorrect, contact HPRCA immediately through the official contact details on hprca.hp.gov.in rather than waiting until exam day

Rajasthan JET 2026: Shift Timings & Reporting Details

Candidates appearing for different papers have been assigned specific shifts, and reaching the centre on time is mandatory for entry. The table below summarises the exam timing and reporting schedule for each category.

Exam/Paper Category Shift Timing Mandatory Reporting Time
First Shift: JET, Pre-PG, and Ph.D. Entrance Exams 11:00 AM – 1:10 PM 9:30 AM (90 minutes prior)

Important: Candidates must reach the exam centre at least 90 minutes before their shift begins, to complete biometric verification, security frisking, and check-in. No candidate is permitted to leave the room from the start of the exam until it ends.

Mandatory Documents Required at the Exam Centre

Entry into the exam hall will be denied without these documents:

  • Admit Card: A clear, printed copy of the Rajasthan JET 2026 hall ticket.

  • Original Photo ID Proof: A valid government-issued ID Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, Driving License, PAN Card, or Passport. Photocopies, digital copies, or coaching institute-issued IDs will not be accepted.

SKRAU has enforced a strict dress code to prevent unfair means during the exam. Candidates should dress according to the following rules to avoid issues at the entry gate.

  • Male candidates: Half-sleeve shirts or T-shirts only; full sleeves are prohibited. All jewellery (rings, chains, earrings, bracelets, etc.) must be removed. Coaching institute uniforms or branded apparel are banned.
  • Female candidates: Half-sleeve kurtas, tops, or blouses only.
  • Footwear: Slippers or low, heel-less sandals only. Shoes and socks are strictly prohibited.
  • Other restrictions: Clothing with large buttons, brooches, or metallic decorations is not allowed.

Rajasthan JET 2026 Exam Pattern & OMR Sheet Rules

Knowing the exam pattern and OMR marking rules in advance helps candidates avoid errors that could lead to disqualification. Here are the key details released by SKRAU:

  • Language: The JET paper is bilingual (English and Hindi), with English prevailing in case of discrepancy. Pre-PG and Ph.D. papers are in English only.
  • 5-Option Rule: Each question has five options (A–E). To answer, candidates darken A, B, C, or D; to skip a question, darkening circle E is mandatory.
  • Marking Scheme: +4 marks for each correct answer, −1 mark for each incorrect answer. Marking more than one option counts as wrong.
  • Stationery: Only the black ballpoint pen provided by the invigilator can be used. Erasers, correction fluid, and blades are strictly forbidden on the OMR sheet; damaged sheets will not be replaced.
  • Subject Selection (JET candidates): Out of 5 available subjects, candidates must attempt only the three subjects they studied/passed in Class 12. Attempting a wrong combination leads to disqualification.

Candidates are advised to preserve their admit card after the exam, as it will be required again during counselling and admission.

  1. Phase 1 - Preliminary Exam (Qualifying) - Online objective CBT | 200 marks | 120 minutes | Negative marking of 0.25 per wrong answer | Qualifying nature only
  2. Phase 2 - Main Exam (Merit-Based) - Objective + Descriptive papers | Papers on Economic & Social Issues (ESI), Finance & Management (F&M), and English | Specialised papers for DEPR/DSIM streams
  3. Phase 3 - Interview - 75 marks | Candidates appear for a Psychometric Test before the interview | Final merit based on Phase 2 + Interview marks

  • Use “Forgot Password” link if needed
  • Check your registered email for confirmation details

Issue #2: City Slip Not Showing / Page Not Loading

Solutions:

  • Verify if city slip is released for your slot
  • Try downloading during non-peak hours (early morning or late night)
  • Disable VPN, proxy, or ad-blocker extensions
  • Check your internet connection stability
  • Try using mobile data instead of WiFi (or vice versa)
  • Use incognito/private browsing mode
  • Update your web browser to the latest version

Solutions:

  • Try “Print to PDF” option (Ctrl+P then save as PDF)

  • Check if pop-ups are blocked in browser settings
  • Ensure sufficient storage space on device
  • Try downloading from different device

Issue #5: Captcha Not Visible or Loading

Solutions:

  • Enable JavaScript in browser settings
  • Disable browser extensions temporarily
  • Use a different browser
  • Clear browser cache completely

Sangli DCC Bank Clerk Eligibility Criteria 2026

Understanding the eligibility criteria is the first step before applying. This section covers educational qualifications, domicile requirements, and other key conditions.

To be considered for the Junior Assistant role, candidates must fulfil all of the following conditions as on the date of application:

Educational Qualification

  • A graduate degree in any discipline from a recognized university.
  • Additionally, candidates must hold an MS-CIT certificate or an equivalent computer course recognized by the Government of Maharashtra (as per Govt. letter no. 277/39 dated 4 Feb. 2013). Accepted equivalents include D.O.A.C.C. and N.E.I.L.L.I.T. New Delhi certificates.
  • Exception: Candidates who are Graduates or Post-Graduates in Computer Science / Information Technology (IT) are exempt from the MS-CIT requirement.

Domicile Requirement

Domicile of Sangli District is mandatory. Candidates must submit a valid domicile certificate at the time of application. As per a Maharashtra Government resolution dated 08/05/2026, 70% of seats are reserved for Sangli District domiciles and 30% are open for candidates from other districts. However, if candidates from other districts are unavailable, those seats will be filled from Sangli domiciles.

Sangli DCC Bank Clerk Age Limit 2026

Age eligibility is calculated as of a specific reference date. Here's what you need to know:

  • Minimum Age: 18 years
  • Maximum Age: 35 years
  • Reference Date: 20/06/2026
  • Candidates must have been born not earlier than 21/06/1991 to be eligible.

Age relaxation, if any, will be governed by applicable rules; candidates should check the official notification for the latest updates.

Sangli DCC Bank Clerk Salary & Probation Details 2026

One of the most searched queries around this recruitment is the salary structure. Here's a breakdown:

During the 12-month probation period, selected clerks will receive a monthly stipend of ₹22,000/-. After successful completion of probation, the candidate will be placed in the bank's regular Clerk grade and will receive full emoluments as per the bank clerk pay scale.

Confirmation into regular service will depend on satisfactory assessment of work performance, attendance records, and confidential reports during the probation period.

The selection process for the Junior Assistant post involves two stages. Understanding this process helps candidates prepare strategically.

Stage 1: Online Examination
All shortlisted applicants will appear for an online computer-based test.

Stage 2: Personal Interview
Candidates who meet the cut-off in the online exam and whose educational documents are verified will be called for a personal interview conducted at Sangli.

The final merit list will be prepared in descending order based on scores obtained across both stages combined.

SSC CGL 2026 – Selection Process

Selection is through a two-tier Computer Based Examination (CBE). Marks scored in CBE conducted in multiple shifts will be normalized as per the procedure published by SSC vide Notice dated 02-06-2025. There is no provision for re-evaluation/re-checking of scores at any stage.

Subject No. of Questions Maximum Marks Time

1 hour 20 min for scribe-eligible PwBD candidates
B. General Awareness 25 50
C. Quantitative Aptitude 25 50
D. English Comprehension 25 50
Total 100 200  

Tier-I consists of Objective Type / MCQ questions, set in English and Hindi (except English Comprehension). Negative marking: 0.50 marks per wrong answer.

Tier-II: Computer Based Examination

Tier-II is conducted in Paper-I, Paper-II, and Paper-III in separate shifts/days.

Paper Section / Subject Questions Marks Duration

Section-II: English Language & Comprehension + General Awareness 45+25 = 70 210 1 hr timer
Section-III: Computer Knowledge Test (qualifying, mandatory) 20 60 15 min
Section-IV: Data Entry Speed Test (DEST) (qualifying, mandatory) - - Session-II: 15 min
Paper-II (JSO / Statistical Investigator only) Statistics 100 200 2 hours
Paper-III (AAO / AAcO only) General Studies (Finance and Economics) 100 200 2 hours

Negative marking in Tier-II: 1 mark per wrong answer in Section-I, II, III of Paper-I; 0.50 marks in Paper-II and Paper-III. Section-III (CKT) and Section-IV (DEST) are qualifying in nature. Candidates must qualify all sections of Paper-I separately. Higher standards of CKT and DEST are set for specific posts (CSS, MEA, AFHQ, SFIO, CBIC, Postal etc.). Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available for PwBD candidates eligible for scribe.

SSC CGL 2026 – Exam Centres

The examination will be conducted through 9 SSC Regions covering all states and union territories. Candidates must choose three examination centres, in order of priority, within the same region.

Competition Level Analysis for SSC CGL 2026

The overall competition level for SSC CGL 2026 is expected to remain very high because the examination attracts a massive number of graduate applicants every year across India. Even with around 12,256 vacancies, the effective competition ratio remains extremely tough for high-demand posts.

  1. Applicant volume is huge: SSC CGL is among the most sought-after central government exams, and premium posts receive intense preference from top scorers.
  2. Tier-I acts as the main screening stage: With negative marking and sectional timing, both speed and accuracy matter. Candidates targeting top posts generally need a very strong Tier-I score.
  3. Tier-II gets post-specific: Specialized posts like JSO and AAO attract a smaller but more qualified pool, making domain preparation more important than raw competition numbers.
  4. DEST and CKT can eliminate candidates: Although qualifying in nature, poor performance in these sections can disqualify otherwise strong candidates for certain posts.
  5. Physical standards create an extra filter: Certain Inspector and Sub Inspector posts require physical and medical fitness standards that are checked separately by user departments.

Who Should NOT Apply for SSC CGL 2026?

  1. Candidates who will not possess a Bachelor's Degree by 01-08-2026.
  2. Candidates who fall outside the age limit for all eligible posts even after applicable relaxation.
  3. OBC Creamy Layer candidates intending to claim OBC reservation.
  4. Candidates who cannot meet post-specific physical or medical standards for the posts they plan to prefer.
  5. Non-matriculate Ex-Servicemen or those who have not completed the required length of service.
  6. Candidates applying for JSO without the required Mathematics or Statistics qualification.
  7. Female candidates applying specifically for BRO vacancies, where only male candidates are eligible.
  8. Distance-learning degree holders without valid UGC-DEB approval for the relevant period.

Common Mistakes / What to Check Before Applying SSC CGL 2026

  1. Not generating a fresh OTR on the new SSC website.
  2. Using a pre-existing photograph instead of live photo capture where required.
  3. Uploading blurred or wrongly sized signature files.
  4. Selecting the wrong reservation category without valid supporting certificate.
  5. Ignoring post-specific standards before locking post preferences.
  6. Choosing JSO or AAO related preferences without being ready for Paper-II or Paper-III.
  7. Skipping Aadhaar-based authentication even when eligible.
  8. Waiting until the final date for application submission.
  9. Missing the answer key objection window after examination.
  10. Confusing the correction window fee structure.

How to Apply for SSC CGL 2026

Candidates must apply online only at https://ssc.gov.in or through the mY SSC mobile application (available on Store). No other mode of application is accepted. Candidates who have not generated OTR on the new website must do so first. Once OTR is generated on the new website, it remains valid for all future examinations on that portal.

Candidates are advised to opt for Aadhaar-based authentication during OTR. Aadhaar-authenticated candidates get significant exemptions: their applications are not rejected for photograph/signature standards, and they need not carry photo ID at the examination venue.

Steps to Apply:

  1. Generate One-Time Registration (OTR) at https://ssc.gov.in (mandatory; use Aadhaar-based authentication if possible)
  2. Complete OTR profile and lock it
  3. Fill the Common Application Form (CAF) including live photograph capture via camera
  4. Upload scanned signature (JPEG/JPG, 10–20 KB, 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm)
  5. Fill the Examination Specific Module (post preferences, exam centre choices - 3 centres within same region in order of priority)
  6. Pay application fee of Rs. 100/- online (if applicable) by 23-06-2026
  7. Preview/Print the application to verify all details before final submission
  8. Use the correction window (29-06 to 01-07-2026) if any correction is needed (chargeable)
  9. Keep printout of application and all documents for at least 3 years

Documents to Keep Ready for Document Verification (after final selection):

  • Matriculation/Secondary School Certificate (proof of date of birth)
  • Mark sheets for all years/semesters of Graduation + Provisional/Degree Certificate
  • SC/ST Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure of the notification)
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure-X); must be valid as on closing date of application
  • EWS Income & Asset Certificate valid for FY 2026–27 (issued based on income for FY 2025–26) in prescribed format (Annexure-XI)
  • PwBD Disability Certificate from competent authority specifying type of disability (as per Annexure-XII to XIII)
  • Ex-Serviceman discharge certificate and other relevant ESM documents
  • Equivalence certificate (for equivalent qualifications other than standard degrees)
  • DEB/UGC approval letter (for Distance Learning degree holders)
  • Certificate of proficiency in State Regional/official language (for AAO/Assistant Audit Officer State Cadre)

Apply Online at: https://ssc.gov.in | Toll Free Helpline: 1800 309 3063

Important Instructions for SSC CGL 2026 Candidates

  • Final allotment is based on merit-cum-preference, and no alternate post will be offered if a candidate fails post-specific standards after allotment.
  • OBC candidates claiming reservation must not belong to the creamy layer as on the closing date of application.
  • EWS certificate must be valid for FY 2026–27 and should be based on income for FY 2025–26.
  • PwBD candidates must choose the correct sub-category in the application form because no later change is allowed.
  • Scribe rules are strict: the scribe must complete OTR, be Aadhaar-authenticated, and cannot assist more than one candidate.
  • Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available to eligible PwBD candidates.
  • Tentative answer keys can be challenged online by paying Rs. 100 per question within the specified period only.
  • No re-evaluation or re-checking of scores is available at any stage.
  • Candidates should preserve the application form and related documents for at least 3 years.
  • Candidature remains provisional until certificates and documents are verified by the Appointing Authority.
  • Fraudulent claims of reservation status may lead to debarment from all SSC examinations.
  • Any update in exam schedule or process will be communicated through the SSC website only.
  • Applications without the required fee, unless exempted, or incomplete applications will be summarily rejected.

RBI Young Professional Recruitment 2026 - Overview

Before diving into the details, here is a complete quick-reference summary of the RBI YP Recruitment 2026 for candidates assessing their fit.

What Is the RBI Young Professional Programme?

The RBI Young Professional programme is a unique initiative by the Reserve Bank of India designed to bring domain specialists into the central bank's functioning on a contractual basis. Unlike recruitment for regular officer grades, this programme targets individuals with specialized postgraduate or technical expertise who can contribute meaningfully to short-to-medium-term policy-related research and analytical assignments.

Selected Young Professionals work within RBI's Central Office Departments in Mumbai, gaining direct exposure to India's most consequential financial, monetary, and regulatory policy decisions. The engagement enriches both the Bank's analytical capacity and the professional development of selected candidates. It is not a pathway to permanent employment at RBI, but it is widely regarded as an extraordinary professional experience within India's financial policy ecosystem.

This section lists every available Young Professional position in RBI's 2026 recruitment drive, along with the respective post code and the Central Office Department where the selected candidate will be placed.

Post-wise Eligibility and Job Profiles: Complete Breakdown

Every RBI Young Professional post has its own educational qualification requirements, desirable experience profile, and distinct job profile. Understanding these differences is critical before applying - using the wrong post code in your email subject line can result in rejection.

1. YP0626DOS01 - Cyber Security and Information Technology Risk

Department: Department of Supervision, Central Office, Mumbai

This role is designed for specialists who can help RBI assess technology risks, digital resilience, and cybersecurity threats across the regulated financial sector.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate degree or equivalent in Cyber Security / Information Security / Computer Science / IT / Data Science / AI or a related field.
  • Desirable Qualifications & Certifications: CISSP, CISM, CEH, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, AWS/Azure Security; published research in IT, Cybersecurity, or Public Policy journals.

Desirable Experience:

  • Cyber security, technology risk management, digital regulation, or fintech
  • Cloud security, cyber resilience, digital transformation projects
  • Experience with financial institutions, regulators, CERTs, or tech companies

What You Will Do: Conduct policy research on cyber security and digital resilience; draft framework documents; analyze cyber incidents and threat intelligence trends; support AI/ML, cloud security, and data governance projects.

2. YP0626DOS02 - Policy Analytics (DoS)

Department: Department of Supervision, Central Office, Mumbai

This data-heavy role requires candidates who can transform complex supervisory data into actionable analytical outputs using advanced tools.

  • Essential Qualification: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech in Computer Science/IT, or Master's degree in Statistics/Data Science.

Desirable Technical Skills:

  • Excel (Power Query, Power Pivot, VBA macros, automation)
  • Power BI (Advanced DAX, interactive dashboards, drill-through functionality)
  • Python (Pandas, NumPy, ETL workflows, automated reporting)
  • Statistics (regression analysis, forecasting, hypothesis testing, predictive modelling)
  • MIS Automation and large multi-source data management

What You Will Do: Extract and analyze supervisory datasets; develop Power BI dashboards; automate recurring MIS reports using VBA and Python; prepare analytical notes and policy briefs for senior management; support RTI/legal matters through structured data review.

3. YP0626DOR01 - Climate Change Risk and Sustainable Finance

Department: Department of Regulation, Central Office, Mumbai

With climate-related financial risks gaining regulatory prominence worldwide, this role positions the selected candidate at the frontier of ESG and sustainable finance regulation in India.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's degree or PG qualification in Climate Change Studies / Environmental Science / Environmental Management / Climate Finance / Sustainability / Economics / Financial Economics / Finance / Statistics / Econometrics / Data Science / Public Policy / Disaster Management / Natural Resource Management / related quantitative disciplines.
  • Desirable Certifications: FRM (GARP), SCR (GARP), ESG-related certifications.
  • Desirable Skills: Knowledge of physical and transition climate risks; understanding of ESG frameworks; Python, R, SQL, Excel, or data visualization tools.
  • What You Will Do: Climate risk research and analysis; policy support and regulatory framework development; climate stress testing; ESG and sustainable finance work; preparation of reports and policy notes; stakeholder engagement and capacity building.

4. YP0626DOR02 - Credit Risk Analytics & Regulatory Policy

Department: Department of Regulation, Central Office, Mumbai

This post is aimed at quantitatively strong candidates who can contribute to credit risk regulation, macroprudential analysis, and evidence-based policy development.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's degree or equivalent in Economics / Econometrics / Statistics / Finance / Mathematics / Data Science / Financial Engineering or related quantitative disciplines.
  • Desirable Qualification: PhD in Finance, Economics, or Statistics; or published research in credit risk or financial stability.
  • Desirable Experience: Risk modelling in financial institutions or credit rating agencies; experience with Python and large datasets; familiarity with ECL/IFRS-9, credit bureau data, BCBS and FSB regulatory standards.
  • What You Will Do: Frame and review credit risk regulations; identify regulatory gaps; support evidence-based policy; analyze international regulatory developments; develop analytical frameworks for assessing the impact of regulatory policies.

5. YP0626DPS01 - Payment Ecosystem

Department: Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Central Office, Mumbai

This role calls for candidates who can track and analyze developments in India's rapidly evolving payment ecosystem, including cross-border payment architectures.

Essential Qualification (any one):

  • PG degree in Economics / Statistics / Finance / Commerce / Public Policy / Data Science
  • B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech
  • Chartered Accountant (CA)

Desirable Experience: Payment systems, cross-border payments, public policy, or financial markets.

What You Will Do: Monitor market intelligence from international bodies (CPMI, FATF, BIS); undertake primary and secondary research on global payment architectures; generate analytical reports for international forums; statistical modelling of payment flow data.

6. YP0626DPS02 - Policy and Research in Domestic & Cross-Border Payment Systems

Department: Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Central Office, Mumbai

This position supports RBI's top management with policy notes, research briefs, and market intelligence covering both domestic and international payment developments.

Essential Qualification (any one):

  • PG degree in Economics / Statistics / Finance / Commerce / Public Policy / Data Science
  • B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech
  • Chartered Accountant (CA)

Desirable Experience: Public policy, payment systems.

What You Will Do: Prepare notes and briefs for RBI's top management on payment system policy; track domestic and international payment ecosystem developments; gather market intelligence from CPMI, FATF, BIS; contribute to research and thematic studies on payment systems.

7. YP0626DEP01 - Policy and Research (DEPR)

Department: Department of Economic and Policy Research, Central Office, Mumbai

This is one of the most academically demanding posts in the RBI YP 2026 recruitment, designed for candidates with strong economics research credentials.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's or PhD in Economics, with at least one course paper in Mathematics, Statistics, or Econometrics during the Master's programme.
  • Desirable Qualification: Authored at least one paper in a reputed journal ranked B or above.
  • Desirable Experience: Economic research; experience with STATA, EViews, Python, or R.
  • What You Will Do: Review research papers and reports on policy and regulatory matters; prepare concise summaries and background notes for RBI's top management; support senior leadership in meetings and presentations.

8. YP0626FIN01 - Artificial Intelligence

Department: FinTech Department, Central Office, Mumbai

As AI transforms the financial sector, RBI seeks a specialist who can shape its approach to AI governance, ethics, and regulatory oversight.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate/technical/professional degree in AI / Computer Science / Public Policy / Data Science or a related discipline.
  • Desirable Knowledge: AI governance, machine learning concepts, data ethics, emerging technology policy frameworks.
  • Desirable Experience: AI research, technology policy, data analysis; exposure to ethical AI frameworks, regulatory research, or public policy projects.
  • What You Will Do: Analyse emerging AI technologies; develop policy recommendations on ethics, governance, data privacy, and responsible AI adoption; support regulatory research and stakeholder consultations; assist in strategy formulation for AI-driven innovation ecosystems.

9. YP0626FIN02 - Quantum Technology

Department: FinTech Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This highly specialized and forward-looking role places a candidate at the cutting edge of India's quantum technology policy landscape.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate/technical/professional degree in Quantum Computing / Physics / Electronics / Computer Science / Technology Policy.
  • Desirable Knowledge: Quantum technologies, cybersecurity implications, innovation policy research.
  • Desirable Experience: Quantum technology research, emerging technology analysis, quantum computing applications, or cybersecurity research.
  • What You Will Do: Conduct research on quantum computing, communication, and cybersecurity trends; assist in developing strategic frameworks for quantum ecosystem development; support standards-setting and international collaboration initiatives.

10. YP0626FMO01 - Data Analysis

Department: Financial Markets Operations Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This role suits a candidate who can translate financial market data into policy-relevant insights, particularly in the money market domain.

  • Essential Qualification: Post Graduation in Statistics / Economics with Econometrics as a subject.
  • Desirable Qualifications: CFA, FRM; proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
  • Desirable Experience: Econometrics; published research; banking dealer experience; money market exposure.
  • What You Will Do: Perform data analysis to support policy research; track domestic and global currency and yield movements; analyze money market rates on a daily basis.

Department: Financial Markets Regulation Department, Central Office, Mumbai

A role for quantitatively oriented professionals who can harness analytical tools to study and interpret financial market behavior for regulatory purposes.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate degree in Economics / Operations Research / Finance / Statistics / Mathematics.
  • Desirable Experience: Any area related to financial markets.
  • What You Will Do: Study and analyze financial market data using cutting-edge analytical tools in close coordination with the regulatory function.

12. YP0626CEP01 - Data Analytics and Policy Research

Department: Consumer Education and Protection Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This role focuses on using data science and machine learning to understand consumer complaint trends and translate them into policy inputs for RBI's leadership.

  • Essential Qualification: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech, or Postgraduate degree in Mathematics / Statistics / Computer Science / Economics / Data Analytics with knowledge of statistical tools and Power BI.
  • Desirable Skills: Python, R, or SQL for automation, machine learning, and large dataset handling.
  • What You Will Do: Data mining and analytics using AI/ML tools; systematic classification of consumer complaints and trends; process automation of report generation; development of interactive real-time dashboards; preparation of quality policy inputs for RBI's top management.

RBI Young Professional Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must satisfy the following baseline conditions to be considered for any of the 12 Young Professional positions at RBI. These are non-negotiable and checked at the time of document verification.

  • Nationality: Must be an Indian citizen.
  • Age Limit: Must be above 21 years and not more than 30 years of age as on July 6, 2026. The notification does not mention any age relaxation for reserved categories under this recruitment.
  • Educational Qualification: Must meet the post-specific eligibility criteria as detailed in Annexure-III of the official notification. All qualifications must be from a recognized institution in India or abroad. In cases of similar or alternative qualifications, RBI retains sole authority to determine equivalency.
  • Agreement to Terms: Candidates must agree to the Terms and Conditions of Engagement as specified in the notification.
  • Application Mode: Must apply via email in the prescribed proforma (Annexure-VI of the official notification).

Each post has its own essential qualification. Meeting the general age criterion alone does not guarantee eligibility - always check the post-specific educational requirement before applying.

Monthly Stipend and Terms of Engagement

Understanding what this role offers - and what it does not - is essential before applying. RBI's YP engagement is a contractual position with a generous stipend but with clearly defined boundaries.

Remuneration

A fixed monthly stipend of ₹1,50,000 will be paid throughout the engagement period, subject to applicable tax deductions. No additional allowances, HRA, or benefits are provided over and above this stipend.

Contract Duration

The initial contract tenure is 3 years, which may be extended by mutual agreement for a total period not exceeding 5 years. The extension decision is based solely on the Bank's assessment of the YP's performance and is at RBI's discretion.

Nature of Engagement

This is a contractual, full-time engagement - not a regular or permanent appointment. The YP will have no claim to any regular or permanent position at RBI by virtue of this engagement. There is no employer-employee relationship between RBI and the YP.

Leave Policy

YPs are entitled to 15 days of leave per calendar year, accrued on a pro-rata basis from the date of joining. Leave cannot be carried forward to the next year. Absence beyond this entitlement is treated as leave without pay, with a proportionate deduction from the monthly stipend. Unauthorized absence for 8 or more consecutive working days without valid reason may lead to contract termination.

Termination and Notice Period

Either party may terminate the contract with 3 months' notice. However, during the first 6 months of the initial tenure, the contract may be terminated by either side without any notice period.

Other Conditions

  • Place of engagement is Mumbai; no residential accommodation will be provided by RBI
  • No part-time work for any private or public body is permitted during the engagement without prior written permission from RBI
  • YPs must produce a medical fitness certificate and a satisfactory police verification report on selection
  • A code of conduct agreement and secrecy undertaking must be signed on joining
  • In the event of death, injury, or illness during tenure, neither the YP nor their dependents are entitled to compensation or employment from RBI

RBI Young Professional Recruitment 2026 Apply Link & Process

The application process for RBI YP 2026 is entirely email-based. There is no online portal, no registration system, and no walk-in interview. Every step must be followed precisely to avoid rejection.

Step 1 - Download the Application Proforma: Download Annexure-VI from the official notification document available at www.rbi.org.in. Fill it out completely. Fields marked with asterisk (*) are mandatory.

Step 2 - Prepare Your Documents: Compile all the following in PDF format:

  • Duly filled application proforma (Annexure-VI) with recent colour photograph (3.5 x 4.5 cm) pasted
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Degree certificates for essential and desirable qualifications (provisional certificate acceptable if the degree is pending)
  • Statement of Interest (explaining why you are applying for the specific post)
  • A sample of academic or policy writing
  • A reference/recommendation letter from a professional referee (preferably from your current/previous employer or academic institution)

Step 3 - Check the Email Specifications:

  • All documents must be in PDF format only - other formats may be blocked by RBI's security filters
  • Total attachment size must not exceed 5 MB
  • The email body must be concise (one or two lines) and unconditional - no additional statements

Step 4 - Format the Email Subject Line Correctly:
The subject line must follow this exact format: "YP Application - [Post Code] - [Your Full Name]"

Eligibility Criteria - Qualification & Experience Required

Each post carries specific educational and professional experience requirements. Read the details for your target role carefully, since 54.9% will not be rounded up to 55% and teaching/freelancing experience is explicitly excluded.

  • Education: B.E. / B.Tech or AMIE or equivalent in Civil Engineering with a minimum of 55% marks.
  • Experience: Minimum 2 years post-qualification executive experience. Gross annual CTC in last/current organisation must be at least ₹3,60,000 per annum.
  • Required: Hands-on site construction experience in Civil/Structural works - Residential, Institutional, or Industrial projects.

Assistant Manager – Electrical (E-1)

Assistant Manager – Mechanical (E-1)

  • Education: B.E. / B.Tech or AMIE or equivalent in Mechanical Engineering with a minimum of 55% marks.

How to Apply Online for EPI Recruitment 2026

All applications must be submitted exclusively through the EPI official website. Applications sent by email or post will not be accepted. Follow each step carefully - no modifications are allowed after final submission.

  1. Visit the official website: Go to www.epi.gov.in and navigate to HRD – Current Openings.
  2. Register yourself: Create a new account with a valid and active email ID that you will monitor throughout the selection process.
  3. Keep documents ready before filling the form:
    • Passport-size colour photograph and signature - JPEG format, maximum 60 KB each.
    • Date of birth, contact and address details, category (UR/OBC/SC/ST/EWS/PWD).
    • Educational details: year of passing, percentage of marks (or equivalent percentage for CGPA).
    • Professional details: company name, duration, post held, area of work, pay scale, and salary details.
  4. Fill the application form carefully: Double-check all entries before submission. No changes are allowed after final submission.
  5. Submit and send documents by email: After submitting the online form, send the system-generated application along with scanned copies of qualification, experience, and salary documents to [email protected].
  6. Print confirmation page: Take a printout of the application confirmation page for future reference.

Shortlisting & Selection Process

EPI uses a merit-based shortlisting process to filter applicants before calling them for interview. Understanding this process helps you assess your competitive standing before applying.

  • Candidates are shortlisted based on percentage of marks in the required qualification and post-qualification experience.
  • Fraction of percentage is ignored - 54.9% is treated as less than 55% and will lead to rejection.
  • If applications are high in volume, EPI may conduct a Written Test before the interview stage.
  • The shortlist will be published on the EPI website; selected candidates will also be informed by email.
  • The final list of selected candidates will be hosted on the EPI website after the interview.
  • Interview venue: Western Regional Office (WRO), Mumbai. No TA/DA is admissible for attending the interview.

  • System-generated application form (printed).

  • Caste/Category certificate: SC/ST/OBC (NCL)/EWS/PWD certificate as applicable from competent authority. OBC (NCL) certificate must not be older than 6 months; EWS certificate must not be older than 1 year from the date of application.
  • Valid photo ID proof - Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID, or Indian Passport.
  • One recent passport-size colour photograph.

CGPA to Percentage Conversion - EPI's Official Rules

If your degree certificate shows CGPA instead of percentage, EPI has specific conversion norms you must follow when filling your application form.

  • If the university provides a conversion formula: Use the university's own conversion and obtain a certificate from the university confirming the equivalent percentage. Submit this certificate at the time of interview.
  • If the university does not provide a conversion formula: A minimum CGPA of 6 on a 10-point scale will be treated as equivalent to 60%. For scales other than 10-point, the score will be prorated accordingly.

Eligibility Criteria for ESIC Professor 2026

Understanding who qualifies is essential before applying. The eligibility conditions differ slightly for medical and non-medical candidates, and both must meet specific experience thresholds recognized by the National Medical Commission (NMC).

Age Limit

  • Maximum age: 50 years as on the closing date (27 July 2026)
  • SC/ST candidates: 5 years relaxation (upper limit: 55 years)
  • OBC candidates: 3 years relaxation (upper limit: 53 years)
  • PwBD candidates: 10 years relaxation (upper limit: 60 years; SC/ST PwBD: 15 years, OBC PwBD: 13 years) - subject to a maximum of 56 years
  • ESIC/Government employees: 5 years relaxation
  • Ex-Servicemen: 5 years relaxation, subject to minimum 6 months service after attestation

Educational Qualifications

For Medical Candidates (Essential):

  1. A recognized medical qualification included in the First or Second Schedule or Part-II of the Third Schedule to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956.
  2. A postgraduate qualification - MD (Doctor of Medicine) or MS (Master of Surgery) or a recognized equivalent in the respective subject or allied discipline.

For Non-Medical Candidates (Essential):

  1. A Master's Degree in the concerned subject or allied discipline.
  2. A Doctorate degree from a recognized university in the respective subject or allied discipline.

Teaching Experience

Candidates must fulfill one of the following:

Option A: Four years of teaching experience as a Reader or Associate Professor in a recognized medical college in the concerned specialty.

Option B: Three years of teaching experience as an Associate Professor in a recognized medical college, plus a minimum of four research publications in indexed or national journals - published as the First Author in journals of National Associations or Societies of the respective specialties. Of these, at least two publications must have been during the tenure as Associate Professor.
