Eligibility Criteria - Qualification and Age Limit

Candidates checking their eligibility for BEML Operator Recruitment 2026 should know that both educational qualification and age are fixed as on 10 July 2026. This section explains the mandatory ITI qualification and the trade-independent age limit applicable across all five posts.

Educational Qualification (Applicable to All Trades)

  • First-class (60%) marks in the respective ITI trade, along with a National Trade Certificate (NTC) issued by the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT)
  • Completion of Apprenticeship with a National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) in the respective trade issued by the Directorate General of Training (DGT)
  • Candidates must have completed the ITI course under the Conventional Training Pattern of the Craftsmen Training Scheme as a regular candidate

Candidates from SC/ST/PwD categories get a 5% relaxation in the minimum qualifying percentage, meaning they need only 55% instead of 60% in their respective trade.

Candidates asking about age relaxation can note that SC/ST candidates get a 5-year relaxation and OBC candidates get a 3-year relaxation over the General age limit. PwD candidates receive an additional 10 years of relaxation over and above the relaxation applicable to their SC/ST/OBC-NCL category, provided they have a minimum 40% disability.

BEML Operator Selection Process 2026 - Step-by-Step

Candidates wondering how BEML will select Operators for these 362 posts can note that the process involves a Computer Based Written Test, document verification, and a pre-employment medical examination, conducted broadly in the sequence below.

  1. Computer Based Written Test: Conducted over 2 hours, with three parts — Part-I: 20 questions on General Awareness, Part-II: 20 questions on English & Reasoning, Part-III: 60 questions on the concerned Discipline. Each question carries 1 mark, and there is no negative marking.
  2. Result and Shortlisting: The qualifying mark is fixed at 45%, relaxed to 40% (5% relaxation) for SC/ST/PwD candidates. Shortlisting is done purely on written test performance.
  3. Document Verification: Candidates are called in order of merit, limited to the number of positions notified per trade/category, where original certificates and one set of self-attested photocopies must be produced.
  4. Travelling Allowance: Candidates who qualify document verification are reimbursed Sleeper Class/II Class train or bus fare by the shortest route, on production of proof of travel.
  5. Provisional Offer and Medical Examination: Candidates clearing document verification receive a Provisional Offer and must undergo a pre-employment medical examination, with no relaxation in health standards.
  6. Final Offer of Engagement: Issued only after a satisfactory medical report is received from the Company's doctor.

Candidates should note that mere fulfilment of eligibility conditions does not guarantee selection, and BEML Management reserves the right to restrict the number of candidates or increase the qualifying percentage based on the volume of applications received.

  6. Pay the applicable application fee online (GEN/EWS/OBC candidates only)

Candidates can use the Apply Online link only until 18:00 Hrs on 10 July 2026, after which the registration site will close. No request for change in category, address, e-mail, mobile number, or test centre location will be entertained once submitted.

Provident Fund is calculated on Basic Pay plus DA, and selected candidates are also entitled to Gratuity (as per the Gratuity Scheme) and Bonus (as per the Bonus Act). Documents Required While Applying Online

Candidates often ask what documents are needed beforehand to avoid application rejection — this section lists every mandatory upload required to complete the BEML Operator online application successfully.

  • Recent photograph and signature (on clear white background, signature in black ink)
  • 10th Standard (X-th) marks card
  • ITI - National Trade Certificate (NTC); provisional certificate accepted if final certificate is not yet issued
  • All ITI marks cards as a single PDF (CGPA-to-percentage conversion certificate required, if applicable)

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many candidates lose out on otherwise eligible applications due to small, avoidable errors. This section highlights frequent mistakes applicants should watch out for while applying for this BEML recruitment.

  • Uploading provisional instead of required documents: NTC provisional certificates are accepted, but candidates should still keep the final certificate ready for the joining stage.
  • Entering an inactive e-mail or mobile number: Since all communication, including offer letters, is sent only via the registered e-mail, candidates should use an ID and number valid for at least one year.
  • Ignoring the OBC-NCL certificate validity: The OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate must not be older than six months as on the last date of online application submission, so candidates should get an updated certificate if their existing one is outdated.
  • Missing the CGPA conversion certificate: Candidates with CGPA/credit-based ITI marksheets must attach the official conversion formula/certificate, or their application may be treated as incomplete.
  • Requesting changes after submission: Category, address, e-mail, mobile number, or test centre preference cannot be modified after submission, so candidates should double-check all entries before the final submit.
  • Applying without verifying eligibility: Only candidates who fully meet the qualification, age, and category criteria as on 10 July 2026 should apply, since candidature found ineligible at any stage will be cancelled, even after appointment.

The application fee is Nil for all categories of candidates applying for these 5 IT positions.

CIBIL Score and Credit History Requirement

Unlike most government job notifications, this Bank of Baroda recruitment includes a specific financial credibility check. This is an important and somewhat unique eligibility condition candidates must be aware of.

Candidates must maintain a satisfactory credit history, and a minimum CIBIL score of 680 or above is required at the time of joining. Candidates who have defaulted on loan repayment or credit card dues, or against whom adverse reports exist from CIBIL or other external credit rating agencies, will be deemed ineligible for appointment. The Bank reserves the right to reject candidature at any stage, including after joining, if the credit profile is found unsatisfactory.

Remuneration and Location of Posting

Salary for these roles is not fixed on a standard pay scale, unlike typical government recruitment. This section explains how pay is determined and where selected candidates will be posted.

Remuneration will be offered based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, overall suitability, last drawn salary, and market benchmark - there is no fixed pay scale mentioned in the notification. The location of posting is Mumbai or Hyderabad, though selected candidates remain liable for transfer anywhere in India as per the Bank's requirement.

Selection Process

Selection for these IT leadership posts goes beyond a standard written exam, with the Bank assessing multiple professional parameters. No fixed exam date or selection timeline has been announced in the notification.

The selection process may include an online test, a psychometric test, or any other test the Bank deems suitable, followed by an Interview or multiple interviews. The Bank may shortlist applications based on criteria such as suitability for the role, depth of prior experience, leadership exposure, domain expertise, professional certifications, and exposure to regulatory or compliance frameworks. The minimum qualifying mark for the Personal Interview (PI) is 60% for UR category and 55% for Reserved category candidates.

How to Apply Online for Bank of Baroda IT Recruitment 2026

Applications for these posts can only be submitted online, with no other mode accepted. Here is the step-by-step process candidates need to follow.

  1. Visit the Bank's official website and go to the Career section → Current Opportunities page.
  2. Register online using the application format enabled for this recruitment.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully, since no changes are allowed after clicking SUBMIT.
  4. Upload your Bio-data, scanned photograph, signature, and supporting eligibility documents as per the prescribed specifications.
  5. Verify all entered details, including name, category, date of birth, and post applied for, before final submission.
  6. Submit the application well before 10-07-2026 to avoid last-minute website load issues.
  7. Save the acknowledgement number generated on the portal and check your registered email for confirmation - registration is complete only once this acknowledgement is received.

Documents and Upload Specifications

Bank of Baroda requires specific documents to be uploaded at the time of application, each with strict file format and size requirements. Getting these specifications wrong is a common reason applications get stuck.

Documents to Upload (Application Stage)

  • Resume (PDF)
  • DOB Proof: 10th marksheet/certificate (PDF)
  • Educational Certificates: relevant mark-sheets/certificates, scanned in a single PDF file
  • Work experience certificates, if applicable (PDF)
  • Caste/Category Certificate, if applicable (PDF)
  • PWD certificate, if applicable (PDF)

Photograph and Signature Specifications

  • Photograph: recent passport-style colour picture, dimensions 200 x 230 pixels, file size between 20kb–50kb.
  • Signature: signed in black ink on white paper, dimensions 140 x 60 pixels, file size between 10kb–20kb.
  • Document files: must be in PDF format, A4 page size, and not exceeding 500 KB each.

Documents Required at Interview Stage

At the time of interview, candidates must produce originals along with self-attested photocopies of documents including the call letter printout, system-generated application printout, date of birth proof, photo identity proof, mark sheets and degree certificates, and category certificates where applicable. Notably, a Ration Card will not be accepted as valid identity proof for this recruitment.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Given the strict, no-correction-after-submission policy of this recruitment, small errors can have a big impact. The following points can help candidates avoid losing their candidature.

  • Do not submit the application without double-checking every field - no changes are allowed once you click SUBMIT.
  • Do not upload a photograph or signature outside the specified pixel and file-size limits, as the system will reject non-compliant files.
  • Do not assume your credit history is irrelevant - a CIBIL score below 680 or any adverse credit report can make you ineligible.
  • Do not delay applying until the last day; server load near the 10-07-2026 deadline can prevent successful submission.
  • Do not carry a Ration Card as your only ID proof for the interview - it will not be accepted.
  • Do not forget to check the position-specific eligibility link for your chosen post, since detailed qualifications differ by role.

Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry Scheme 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must fulfill all eligibility conditions as on the date of application. Only unmarried men and women fulfilling the conditions of nationality as laid down by the Government of India are eligible. Any candidate found to be married or who marries while under training will be discharged from service and shall be liable to refund full training cost including pay, allowances and any other expenditure incurred by the Government.

Criteria Details
Nationality As per conditions of nationality laid down by the Government of India.
Marital Status Unmarried men and women only. Candidates who marry while under training will be discharged and must refund all training costs.
Educational Qualification Passed Senior Secondary Examination (10+2 pattern) or equivalent from any recognized Board with at least 70% aggregate marks in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM) and at least 50% marks in English (either in Class X or Class XII).
JEE (Main) 2026 Requirement Must have appeared for JEE (Main) 2026 exam (for B.E./B.Tech). Call up for SSB will be issued on the basis of JEE (Main) All India Common Rank List (CRL) 2026 published by NTA. Candidates must fill their CRL Rank in the application.
Medical Standards All candidates recommended by SSB must undergo medical examination applicable to 10+2 (B.Tech) entry. Change of medical hospital/centre is not permissible under any circumstances.
Narcotics Use/possession of narcotics is banned. Candidates may be tested during SSB/medicals/training/service. If found using/possessing narcotics at any stage, candidate will be debarred from joining or removed from service.

Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry Scheme 2026 - Selection Process

Selection will be based on JEE (Main) 2026 CRL-based shortlisting, followed by SSB Interview, Medical Examination, and Police & Character Verification. Merit list will be prepared based on SSB marks and medical fitness. Candidates will be appointed subject to Police Verification, Character Verification, and availability of vacancies in the entry. Mere inclusion in the common merit list does not confer a vested right to appointment. Mere empanelment under no circumstances can be treated as final selection.

Stage 1 - Shortlisting Based on JEE (Main) 2026 CRL

Naval Headquarters reserves the right to fix the cut-off for shortlisting of applications for SSB based on JEE (Main) All India Common Rank List (CRL) 2026. All candidates must fill their CRL Rank in the application. Shortlisted candidates will be informed about their SSB interview schedule through email and SMS. Candidates must not change their email/mobile number until the selection process is over.

Stage 2 - Service Selection Board (SSB) Interview

SSB interviews for shortlisted candidates will be scheduled at Bengaluru / Bhopal / Kolkata / Visakhapatnam from September 2026 onwards. Change of SSB Centre is not permissible under any circumstances. Candidates must download the call-up letter on receiving intimation from Naval Headquarters via SMS/email. AC 3-tier rail fare is admissible for SSB interview if appearing for the first time for this particular type of commission - candidates must bring a photocopy of the first page of passbook or cheque leaf with Name, A/C No., and IFSC details. No compensation is admissible in case of any injury sustained during SSB tests.

Stage 3 - Medical Examination

All candidates recommended by SSB must undergo medical examination as per standards applicable to 10+2 (B.Tech) entry. No relaxation in medical standards on any grounds. Candidates already declared medically fit for NDA/INA Jan 27 need not repeat medical examination. Change of medical hospital/centre is not permissible under any circumstances.

Stage 4 - Common Merit List & Appointment

Final merit list will be prepared based on SSB marks and medical fitness. Candidates will be appointed subject to Police Verification, Character Verification, and availability of vacancies. All vacancies are to be filled as per service requirement and statutory guidelines issued from time to time.

Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech Cadet Entry Scheme 2026 - Training Details

Selected candidates will be inducted as Cadets for the four-year B.Tech Course at the Indian Naval Academy (INA), Ezhimala, in Electronics & Communication Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Naval Architecture & Shipbuilding (only for 07 selected candidates from Mechanical Engineering at NCW, Kochi) as per Naval requirements. On completion of the course, B.Tech Degree will be awarded by Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU). The entire cost of training including books and reading material will be borne by the Indian Navy. Cadets will also be provided with entitled clothing and messing. Details of pay, allowances, group insurance, gratuity, leave entitlements, and duties of officers are available on www.joinindiannavy.gov.in.

About SDSC SHAR and the Space Central Schools

This section explains who SDSC SHAR is and why it is hiring teachers, which helps candidates understand the nature of the employer before applying.

Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota (SDSC SHAR) is India's spaceport, functioning under the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Department of Space, Government of India. It is located 100 km north of Chennai on National Highway 05, in Tirupati District, Andhra Pradesh. SDSC SHAR operates Space Central Schools at its Sriharikota and Sullurpeta campuses under the NCERT/CBSE curriculum, primarily to educate the children of its employees and supporting personnel. To staff these schools, SDSC SHAR has invited online applications for five categories of teaching posts.

Post-Wise Vacancy Details (10 Posts)

Candidates checking how many posts are open and in which subject can refer to the table below, which lists all five post codes notified by SDSC SHAR along with their reserved category and vacancy count.

Post Code Post Name Vacancies & Category

04 Trained Graduate Teacher (Telugu) ST-01
05 Primary Teacher UR-03, EWS-01, OBC-02 (1 OBC backlog)

Of the six Primary Teacher vacancies, one post is identified for PwBD (LDCP) backlog vacancy. If a suitable PwBD (LDCP) candidate is not found, the post will be offered to a candidate with any other benchmark disability except blindness, and if still unfilled, it will revert to the vertical reservation category. All posts are currently temporary in nature but are likely to continue.

Eligibility Criteria for Each Teaching Post

Each post carries a distinct qualification requirement linked to the subject taught. The table-style breakdown below summarises the core academic and teaching-eligibility requirements for every post code.

TGT (Maths) - To Teach Maths and Physics

Candidates need a four-year NCTE-recognised integrated degree with at least 50% marks (subject + B.Ed component), OR a Bachelor's/Honours degree with 50% marks plus a B.Ed degree from an NCTE-recognised institution (alternatives include a 3-year integrated B.Ed-M.Ed or a 1-year B.Ed Special Education from RCI). Candidates must also have qualified CTET Paper-II and be able to teach in Hindi and English. Applicants must have studied Mathematics as a main subject for at least 3 years/6 semesters, Physics for at least 1 year/2 semesters, and one of Chemistry/Electronics/Computer Science/Statistics for at least 1 year/2 semesters. Candidates with B.Sc (Hons.) in Physics or Chemistry are not eligible for this post.

TGT (Science) - To Teach Chemistry and Biology

The qualification pattern mirrors TGT (Maths): a four-year integrated degree or a Bachelor's/Honours degree (50% marks) with Chemistry, plus a B.Ed degree, along with a qualifying CTET Paper-II score. Candidates must have studied Biology/Life Science/Botany/Zoology as a Honours or main subject for at least 3 years/6 semesters, combined with Chemistry, Botany, or Zoology as applicable for at least one year or two semesters.

TGT - Work Experience Teacher (WET)

This post requires a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or Electronics & Communication Engineering with at least 50% marks, along with a B.Ed degree (50% marks) from an NCTE-recognised institution, ability to teach in Hindi and English, and knowledge of computers. One year of practical workshop/factory experience is desirable but not mandatory.

TGT (Telugu)

Candidates need a Bachelor's degree with Telugu as the main subject (or one of three equal optional subjects), a BOL in Telugu, or a Postgraduate degree in Telugu, combined with a B.Ed with Telugu methodology or Telugu Pandit Training. Candidates must have passed State TET or CTET Paper-II with Telugu as one of the chosen subjects.

Primary Teacher

Eligible candidates need Senior Secondary/Intermediate (10+2) with 50% marks plus a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education, OR Class XII with 50% marks plus a 4-year B.El.Ed, OR Class XII with 50% marks plus a 2-year RCI Diploma in Special Education. A qualifying score in CTET Paper-I and the ability to teach in Hindi and English are also required.

Across all posts, Hindi working knowledge is necessary, and candidates claiming equivalent qualifications must produce documentary evidence at the time of the Skill Test.

Selection Process: Written Test and Skill Test

SDSC SHAR shortlists and selects teachers through a two-stage process - a written exam followed by a practical skill demonstration - explained below with the exact marking scheme.

Written Test (CBT)

The Computer Based Test checks both the theoretical and practical knowledge of candidates across the prescribed syllabus. For Primary Teacher, TGT (Maths), TGT (Science), and TGT (WET), the paper carries 180 marks split into four parts - Languages (20), General Awareness/Reasoning/Computers (20), Education & Leadership Perspective (40), and Subject Specific (100). For TGT (Telugu), the 180-mark paper covers General English/Awareness/Reasoning (20), Education Perspectives (20), Pedagogy (40), and Telugu Language & Literature (100).

Post Subject-Wise Question Split Minimum Qualifying Marks

TGT (Science) 40% Biology + 30% Chemistry + 30% Physics 40% each subject; 50% aggregate

Based on Written Test performance, candidates are shortlisted for the Skill Test, generally in a 1:5 ratio with a minimum of 10 candidates category-wise.

Skill Test

The Skill Test is purely qualifying in nature, evaluated out of 100 marks, with a minimum qualifying score of 60%. It is a chalk-and-board based test where each candidate is given a subject-related topic and must demonstrate subject knowledge and teaching ability by conducting a mock class.

Final Merit and Tie-Breakers

Final selection is based purely on Written Test marks among candidates who clear the Skill Test, with empanelment done as per the number of notified vacancies. In case of a tie, the academic score of the essential qualification (PG/Graduation/Senior Secondary, as applicable) is the first tie-breaker, followed by the candidate's age (senior candidates get preference) as the second tie-breaker.

  5. Pay the Rs. 750 fee online (no other payment mode is accepted).
  6. Submit the application and download the registration confirmation form for future reference.

A separate application and separate fee payment is mandatory for each post; candidates cannot submit multiple applications for the same post, and incomplete applications will not be entertained.

Bank of Baroda Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Apply Online

Applications for this recruitment can be submitted only through the online mode on Bank of Baroda's official website - no offline or postal applications are accepted. The application window is open from 16 June 2026 to 06 July 2026, and registration is complete only once the application fee is successfully paid through the online payment gateway. Candidates can access the application form directly at www.bankofbaroda.bank.in/Career.htm, under the Career section's "Current Opportunities" page on www.bankofbaroda.bank.in.

  • Direct Link to apply Bank of Baroda Professionals Recruitment 2026

Key Roles and Responsibilities

A few common themes run across most of these positions. The Vice President and Deputy Vice President-level Relationship Head and Senior Relationship Manager roles centre on growing and managing the bank's existing corporate relationships in their specialised segment - real estate, MNCs, credit-lite clients, or conglomerates - sourcing new-to-bank corporate clients, cross-selling fee-based products such as forex and cash management services, and building account plans with opportunity-income analysis while keeping risk exposure within the bank's Exposure Risk Framework. The Transaction Banking roles (Head-Product Sales, Senior Product Sales Manager, and Product Sales Manager) focus on selling trade, forex, and cash management products, managing transaction banking client relationships, and driving fee income and CASA balances. The AVP-level Conglomerate/Real Estate and Credit Lite roles concentrate on credit appraisal, risk evaluation, and timely account monitoring, while the DVP-Head Market Intelligence Unit role is centred on gathering and summarising market and industry intelligence to provide competitive insights to management. Across all positions, the bank has reserved the right to modify or add to these responsibilities at any time.

Application Fee

Bank of Baroda has set a two-tier, non-refundable application fee for this recruitment. Unreserved (UR), EWS, and OBC candidates must pay Rs 850 (inclusive of GST), plus applicable payment gateway charges, while SC, ST, PWD, Ex-servicemen/DESM, and Women candidates pay Rs 175 (inclusive of GST), plus payment gateway charges. The fee can be paid online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI. It is payable irrespective of whether an online test is eventually conducted and irrespective of whether the candidate is shortlisted for an interview, and once paid, it will not be refunded under any circumstances.

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

Contract Tenure, Remuneration and Credit Score Requirement

These are fixed-term contractual roles, and the tenure depends on the grade. For AVP I and AVP II, the initial contract runs for 5 years from the date of joining and can be renewed at the bank's discretion, subject to satisfactory performance, for one additional period of up to 5 years. For VP and DVP, the initial contract is for 3 years and can be extended in increments of 1 year each, provided the total engagement does not exceed 5 years. In every case, the engagement automatically ends at contract expiry unless renewed, and it cannot continue beyond the candidate reaching 60 years of age.

Remuneration is not fixed in the notification - the bank states it will be decided based on the selected candidate's qualifications, experience, overall suitability, last drawn salary, and the prevailing market benchmark for the position, and the place of posting will depend on the bank's requirement at any of its offices or branches in India.

A distinctive eligibility condition for this recruitment is credit history: candidates must have a CIBIL score of 680 or above at the time of joining, and the bank has explicitly stated that candidates who have defaulted on loan or credit card repayments, or against whom adverse reports exist with CIBIL or other credit-rating agencies, will be deemed ineligible for appointment - a check the bank can apply at any stage, including after joining.

Selection Process

Selection proceeds through Application Scrutiny, followed by an Online Test, Psychometric Test, or any other test the bank considers suitable, and then a Personal Interview along with compensation negotiation for those selected. The Psychometric Test and/or Interview assess a candidate's personality, communication, clarity, problem-solving ability, efficiency, and willingness to work anywhere in the country. To qualify in the Personal Interview, a candidate must score at least 60% for the Unreserved category and 55% for Reserved category candidates, though the bank reserves the right to revise this cut-off. If multiple candidates tie at the cut-off mark, they are ranked in descending order of age, meaning the older candidate ranks higher.

Call letters will be sent only to the email ID registered in the online application - no hard copies will be sent by post or courier - so candidates must keep that email account active and check it regularly. At the interview, candidates must carry a valid photo ID such as a PAN card, passport, driving licence, voter's card, or Aadhaar card with photograph; a Ration Card will not be accepted as identity proof for this recruitment, and candidates who have legally changed their name must produce the original Gazette notification or affidavit reflecting the new name.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Visit the Bank of Baroda website www.bankofbaroda.bank.in (or directly www.bankofbaroda.bank.in/Career.htm) and go to the Career section's "Current Opportunities" page.
  2. Register using a valid personal email ID and contact number that you can keep active throughout the recruitment process, since all call letters and updates will be sent there.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully - no field can be edited once you click Submit - and ensure your name is spelt exactly as it appears on your certificates and mark sheets.
  4. Upload your bio-data, scanned photograph (200×230 pixels, 20-50 KB), and signature (140×60 pixels, 10-20 KB) in JPG/JPEG format, along with PDF copies of your eligibility documents.
  5. Pay the applicable application fee online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI through the integrated payment gateway.
  6. After successful payment, download and print the system-generated e-receipt and application form for your records; if a transaction fails, register again and make the payment afresh rather than assuming the first attempt succeeded.
  7. Complete the process well before 06 July 2026, since the bank has advised against waiting until the last date to avoid login failures caused by heavy website traffic.

Documents Required (Upload and Interview)

Two separate sets of documents matter here - what must be uploaded with the online application, and what must be physically produced at the interview.

Documents to upload (PDF format, A4 page size, file size not exceeding 500 KB each):

  • Resume
  • Date of Birth proof (10th mark sheet/certificate)
  • Educational certificates (all relevant mark sheets and certificates scanned into a single PDF)
  • Work experience certificates, if applicable
  • Caste/Category certificate, if applicable
  • PWD certificate, if applicable

Documents to carry to the interview (originals plus a self-attested photocopy):

  • Printout of the valid interview call letter and the system-generated online application form
  • Proof of date of birth (birth certificate or SSLC/Class X mark sheet showing DOB)
  • Photo ID proof (PAN, passport, driving licence, voter's card, or Aadhaar with photograph - a Ration Card is not accepted)
  • Semester/year-wise mark sheets and the final degree/diploma certificate
  • Caste certificate in the prescribed Government of India format for SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates (the OBC certificate must include the non-creamy-layer clause and be issued within one year of the date of advertisement)
  • Disability certificate from the District Medical Board for PWD candidates, along with scribe details if a scribe was used
  • Discharge book, pension payment order, and rank proof for Ex-servicemen candidates
  • A No Objection Certificate from the current employer for candidates serving in Government, Quasi-Government, or Public Sector roles, including nationalised banks

Bank of Baroda has also appended ready-to-use certificate formats for SC/ST, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), Persons with Disabilities (single and multiple disability), and EWS candidates as annexures to the notification; candidates applying under these categories should get their certificates issued in this prescribed format from the competent authority.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Keep your scanned photograph between 20-50 KB and your signature between 10-20 KB, both in JPG/JPEG format - files outside this range, or in the wrong format, will trigger an error and block submission. Sign only in your normal handwriting and never in capital letters, since the bank has specified that signatures in capital letters will not be accepted, and any mismatch between your call-letter signature and your interview-day signature can lead to disqualification.

If an online payment fails or you are unsure whether it went through, do not assume it succeeded - register again and complete the payment, since the fee is non-refundable. Use an updated browser and a stable internet connection while filling the form, and avoid waiting until the last day or last few hours before 06 July 2026, since heavy website traffic close to the deadline is a common cause of failed submissions. Always download and save your acknowledgement number, e-receipt, and printed application form immediately after payment, as these are needed for future reference and at the interview. Finally, double-check every field - especially your name, category, and date of birth - before clicking Submit, since no corrections are allowed after the online application has been submitted.

Bank of Baroda is hiring for 86 vacancies across 5 officer-level posts in its Corporate and Institutional Credit (C&IC) department, ranging from Manager to Chief Manager grade in both Credit Analyst and C&IC Relationship roles. Online registration opened on 16 June 2026, and the last date to apply and pay the fee is 6 July 2026. Eligible candidates need a postgraduate finance qualification or CA/CMA/CS/CFA, relevant banking credit experience, and willingness to serve anywhere in India.

Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026: Key Dates You Need to Know

This recruitment drive was announced under advertisement number BOB/HRM/REC/ADVT/2026/10. There are only two dates that matter for candidates: when the application window opens and when it closes, since the bank has not yet announced an online test date.

86 Vacancies Across 5 Posts: Full Position-wise Breakdown

The 86 vacancies are divided into two job families: Credit Analyst posts and C&IC Relationship posts, each spanning three or two seniority grades respectively. Vacancy count, age limit, and required post-qualification experience vary by grade, so candidates should check the exact post they qualify for before applying.

Credit Analyst Posts (Manager, Senior Manager & Chief Manager)

Credit Analyst posts focus on appraising corporate credit proposals and carry the highest vacancy count in this recruitment, with the Senior Manager grade alone accounting for 38 of the 86 total seats.

C&IC Relationship Posts (Senior Manager & Chief Manager)

C&IC Relationship posts are client-facing roles centred on sourcing and managing corporate borrowers rather than appraising proposals, and together they account for 43 of the 86 vacancies.

Eligibility Criteria: Qualification, Age & Work Experience

The educational qualification for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026 is identical across all 5 posts, while the age limit and experience requirement increase with seniority. Candidates should also note that the bank will only consider qualifications from institutions recognised by the Government of India or bodies like the AICTE.

  • Educational Qualification: Graduation in any discipline, plus a Post Graduate Degree or Diploma with specialisation in Finance (or its equivalent), OR a professional qualification such as CA, CMA, CS, or CFA.
  • Age: Calculated as on 1 June 2026, ranging from a minimum of 25 years (Manager grade) to a maximum of 42 years (Chief Manager grade).
  • Nationality: Indian citizens are eligible, along with certain categories of Nepali, Bhutanese, Tibetan refugee, and Indian-origin candidates from specified countries, subject to an eligibility certificate from the Government of India where applicable.
  • Posting Condition: Only candidates willing to serve anywhere in India should apply, since the bank can post selected officers to any branch or office at its discretion.

Reservation in Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026 is applied separately for each of the 5 posts rather than as one combined pool, and candidates cannot change their declared category after registering online. CIBIL Score Requirement: A Credit History Check Unique to This Recruitment

Unlike most government recruitment notifications, this advertisement makes personal credit history a formal eligibility condition. Candidates need a minimum CIBIL score of 680 at the time of joining the bank, since this post involves handling corporate credit decisions.

Anyone who has defaulted on loan repayments or credit card dues, or who has adverse reports from CIBIL or other external credit assessment agencies, will be treated as ineligible for appointment. The bank has reserved the right to reject a candidate's selection at any stage, including after joining, if their credit profile turns out to be unsatisfactory.

Probation Period and Mandatory Service Bond

Selected candidates do not join in a permanent capacity immediately; they first complete a probation period, and they must also commit to a minimum service period backed by a financial bond.

  • Probation Period: 12 months (1 year) of active service from the date of joining.
  • Service Bond: Candidates must serve the bank for a minimum of 3 years from the date of joining, or pay ₹5 lakh in lieu of completing the bond period.

The exact bond terms will be confirmed in each selected candidate's offer letter and are subject to revision as per the bank's prevailing policy.

Application Fee for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026

Selection Process: Online Test, Psychometric Assessment & Interview

Selection for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026 can include application scrutiny, an online test, a psychometric assessment, a group discussion, and a personal interview, though the bank retains the right to skip or modify any stage. Final selection depends on combined performance across whichever stages are actually conducted.

Online Test Pattern (Tentative)

If a written test is held, it will be a 150-mark, 150-minute online exam split into four sections, three of which only need to be passed rather than scored well in.

Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Professional Knowledge will be available bilingually in English and Hindi, while the English Language section will be in English only. Sections 1 to 3 are qualifying only and do not count toward the final score; candidates need at least 40% in General/EWS or 35% in Reserved categories to clear each of these sections, and there is no negative marking anywhere in the test.

Personal Interview & Final Merit

Candidates who clear the online test (or are otherwise shortlisted) move on to a psychometric assessment and/or personal interview, where the minimum qualifying score is 60% for General category and 55% for Reserved category candidates. If two or more candidates tie at the cut-off mark, the older candidate is ranked higher in the merit list.

The online test, if conducted, is tentatively planned across more than two dozen cities, including Mumbai, Delhi/NCR, Bangalore, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar, Jaipur, Lucknow, Baroda, Bhopal, Chandigarh-Mohali, and several other regional centres, with the final allotted centre confirmed in the call letter.

Step-by-Step Guide: How to Apply Online

Bank of Baroda accepts applications for this recruitment only through its official website; no offline or postal applications will be considered.

  1. Visit www.bankofbaroda.bank.in and navigate to the Careers section, then Current Opportunities.
  2. Register using a valid personal email ID and contact number that you can keep active until the recruitment process is complete.
  3. Fill in personal, educational, and work experience details carefully, since no changes are allowed once the form is submitted.
  4. Upload your photograph (200 x 230 pixels, 20-50 KB) and signature (140 x 60 pixels, 10-20 KB) in JPG/JPEG format, signed in your normal handwriting and not in capital letters.
  5. Upload your resume, Date of Birth proof, educational certificates (combined in one PDF), and category/PWD/experience certificates where applicable, each as a PDF on A4 size not exceeding 500 KB.
  6. Pay the applicable application fee online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI.
  7. Save and print the system-generated application form and fee receipt for your future reference.

Apply Online for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026

Job Profile: What Will You Actually Do in This Role?

The two job families under this recruitment involve noticeably different day-to-day work, which is worth understanding before choosing which post to apply for.

Credit Analyst roles (Manager/Senior Manager/Chief Manager) are appraisal-focused: examining new and existing corporate credit proposals, conducting credit due-diligence on financial, industry, and business risk, coordinating with Relationship Managers, and ensuring compliance in corporate accounts.

C&IC Relationship roles (Senior Manager/Chief Manager) are client-facing: maintaining relationships with existing corporate clients, sourcing new-to-bank corporate borrowers, cross-selling ancillary business, and creating account plans with opportunity income analysis for corporate borrowers.

Mistakes That Could Cost You This Opportunity

Several avoidable errors can disqualify an otherwise eligible candidate from Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026, so it helps to check these before hitting submit.

  • Assuming any postgraduate degree qualifies - only a finance-specialised PG degree/diploma or a CA/CMA/CS/CFA qualification meets the educational criteria.
  • Not checking your CIBIL score in advance - a score below 680, or any default history, can lead to rejection even after selection.
  • Counting clerical-cadre banking experience toward the eligibility criteria, which is explicitly excluded.
  • Including work experience of less than 6 months from a previous organisation, which will not be counted unless it is part of your current employment.
  • Submitting more than one application - only the latest valid one is retained, and fees paid for earlier ones are forfeited.
  • Selecting a category casually, since no change of category is allowed after registration and an invalid OBC/EWS claim without supporting certificates can affect your candidature.
  • Overlooking the 3-year/₹5 lakh service bond commitment before deciding whether to accept the role if selected.
  • Waiting until the last date to register, risking last-minute website load issues for which the bank takes no responsibility.

  6. Preview the complete application using the "Preview Tab" and verify all entries.
  7. Click "COMPLETE REGISTRATION" after final verification.
  8. Proceed to the Payment Tab and pay the application fee online.
  9. Click "Submit" and save/print the e-Receipt and application form for future reference.

Only one application per candidate is allowed. In case of multiple applications, only the latest will be retained and earlier fees will be forfeited.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many applicants lose their candidature due to avoidable errors during or after the application process. Review the following checklist before submitting your form.

  • Applying for multiple posts: MSC Bank allows one application per candidate. Submit only one application for the post you are most qualified for.
  • Wrong photograph format: Passport-style colour photo against a light background is required. Selfies, group photos, or blurred images will lead to rejection.
  • Signature in CAPITAL LETTERS: Signatures in block/capital letters are strictly rejected. Sign in your normal cursive style with black ink.
  • Missing Domicile Certificate: Only Maharashtra residents can apply. Ensure your Domicile Certificate is valid and ready for document verification.
  • Not checking Marathi in SSC: All posts require Marathi as a subject in Matriculation. Check your mark sheet before applying.
  • Pressing Back/Refresh during payment: After submitting payment information, do not press Back or Refresh. Wait for the server confirmation to avoid double charges.
  • Incomplete scanning of thumb impression: The left thumb impression must be properly scanned and not smudged. A blurred or partial impression can invalidate your application.
  • Not saving the e-Receipt: If an e-Receipt is not generated, the transaction may have failed. Log in again and repeat the payment process.

Punjab and Sind Bank Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

The application fee is non-refundable. Payment must be made online only - cash, cheques, money orders, and postal stamps are not accepted. Bank transaction charges for the online payment gateway are borne by the candidate.

Once submitted, an application cannot be withdrawn, and the fee will not be refunded under any circumstances, nor held in reserve for any other examination.

Punjab and Sind Bank Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

The bank will use a multi-stage selection process for all posts. All three scales - SMGS IV, MMGS III, and MMGS II - follow the same procedure: Written Test → Short-listing → Personal Interview.

The written test, where conducted, will have the following structure:

Section Questions Maximum Marks Duration
English Language 20 20 15 minutes
General Awareness 20 20 30 minutes
Professional Knowledge 60 60 60 minutes
Total 100 100 105 minutes

The minimum qualifying score in each section is 40% for General and EWS candidates and 35% for Reserved Category candidates. However, only Professional Knowledge marks are used for drawing the merit/rank list and shortlisting candidates for the Personal Interview; marks in English Language and General Awareness are not included in the final merit calculation.

Candidates clearing the written test are called for a Personal Interview. The minimum qualifying score for the interview is 40% for Unreserved and EWS candidates and 35% for Reserved categories. Final selection is based on the combined marks from the written test and Personal Interview, in order of merit ranking. Where two candidates tie at the cut-off, they are ranked in descending order of age.

The Personal Interview will be conducted in New Delhi unless otherwise specified. Call letters will be sent by email only. Candidates must attend at their own cost.

The bank shortlists candidates based on experience and suitability at its own discretion - meeting the minimum qualification does not guarantee an interview call.

Examination Centres

The bank has designated examination centres across India. Candidates may opt for a centre in their state, subject to availability. The bank reserves the right to allot a different centre or cancel/add centres. No request for a change of examination centre, date, or session will be entertained. Selected centres include: Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), Guwahati (Assam), Patna and Bhagalpur (Bihar), Chandigarh/Mohali, Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Delhi/Delhi-NCR, Panaji (Goa), Ahmedabad/Gandhinagar (Gujarat), Ambala (Haryana), Hamirpur (Himachal Pradesh), Jammu (J&K), Bengaluru (Karnataka), Ernakulam (Kerala), Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), Mumbai/Thane/Navi Mumbai/MMR (Maharashtra), Bhubaneswar (Odisha), Patiala (Punjab), Jaipur (Rajasthan), Chennai (Tamil Nadu), Hyderabad (Telangana), Prayagraj, Lucknow and Meerut (Uttar Pradesh), Dehradun (Uttarakhand), and Asansol and Siliguri (West Bengal), among others.

Terms of Contract

This engagement is on a contractual basis, not a regular/permanent appointment. The initial period is three years, subject to annual performance review. Depending on need and performance, the bank may extend the contract on an annual basis for up to a maximum of two additional years at its discretion.

The bank may terminate the contract at any time without assigning any reason by giving one month's notice or paying one month's fixed component of compensation in lieu. Similarly, the appointee must give the bank one month's clear notice - or equivalent payment - to exit the contract before its expiry.

Additional conditions: the selected individual must not take up any assignment with any other organization during the contract period; no vigilance case or adverse observation from previous employers should be pending; and the candidate must have a minimum CIBIL score of 650 at the time of joining.

How to Apply

Applications are accepted online only through the bank's official website. The steps below reflect the application flow described in the notification.

  1. Visit https://punjabandsind.bank.in/ and navigate to the Recruitment section on the home page.
  2. Click on the relevant notification for Cloud CoE / AI Engineers.
  3. Before starting registration, scan and prepare the following files:
    • Passport-size photograph (4.5 cm × 3.5 cm; 20–50 KB; JPG/JPEG/PNG)
    • Signature on white paper in black ink (10–20 KB)
    • Left thumb impression on white paper (20–50 KB; JPG/JPEG)
    • Hand-written declaration in English, on white paper in black ink - text: "I, [Name], hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required." (50–100 KB; JPG/JPEG; NOT in capital letters)
    • Supporting documents in PDF format: Brief Resume, ID Proof, Age Proof, Educational Certificates, Experience Certificates/NOC, Caste Certificate (if applicable)
  4. Complete the online registration form. Keep the registered email ID and mobile number active throughout the process.
  5. Upload all documents at the specified fields. The system will not proceed until photographs and signatures meet specifications.
  6. Pay the application fee online. Transaction charges are borne by the candidate.
  7. Submit the application and save/print the system-generated application form with the registration number.
  8. Apply separately for each post if applying for more than one position.

In case of multiple submissions for the same post, only the last valid completed application will be retained; fees paid for earlier submissions will be forfeited.

Documents Required at Document Verification

Candidates called for the interview stage must bring originals and self-attested photocopies of all relevant documents. Documents not produced on the day of verification will disqualify the candidate from further participation.

Required documents include: Date of Birth proof (SSC/School Leaving Certificate); printout of call letter; system-generated online application printout; all educational certificates and mark sheets from Class X onwards (semester-wise mark sheets and provisional/final degree certificate); all work experience certificates and NOC from the current employer if employed with a public sector bank or government/quasi-government organization; caste/category certificates in the prescribed Government of India format (OBC certificate must be no more than one year old and contain the non-creamy layer clause); disability certificate from District Medical Board (if applicable); Income and Asset Certificate (for EWS candidates, valid as on the date of application); two passport-size photographs identical to the one in the application; and valid photo identity proof (PAN Card, Passport, Driving Licence, Voter's Card, Aadhaar, Employee ID, etc. - Ration Card and Learner's Driving Licence are not accepted).

No documents should be sent directly to the bank before or after the interview.

Troubleshooting & Common Mistakes

Photo/Signature upload errors are among the most common reasons for application failure. Ensure your photograph is between 20 KB and 50 KB and your signature between 10 KB and 20 KB. Files larger than the specified limit will be rejected by the system. Use a scanner set to at least 200 DPI and save files in JPG/JPEG format. All supporting documents must be in PDF format.

Payment gateway failures can occur during high-traffic periods near the deadline. If a payment is deducted but the fee status is not updated, wait 24 hours and check again before attempting re-payment; duplicate payments are generally not refunded. Avoid applying on the last day to reduce the risk of server overload.

Hand-written declaration errors are a unique pitfall in this recruitment. The declaration must be in English, in the candidate's own handwriting, in lowercase (not capital letters). A typed or third-party-written declaration will invalidate the application.

Name mismatches between the application and identity documents can cause disqualification at any stage. Ensure the name (and father's/husband's name where applicable) is spelled exactly as it appears on your certificates and mark sheets. Candidates who have changed their name must produce an original Gazette notification, marriage certificate, or affidavit.

CIBIL score is a condition of joining, not selection. Candidates are advised to check their CIBIL score before applying - a score below 650 will disqualify them at the time of joining even if selected.

Ex-Servicemen:

  • Ex-Serviceman means a person who has served in any rank (combatant or non-combatant) in the Central Armed Forces (Army, Navy, Air Force) - excluding persons who served in Defence Security Corps, General Reserve Engineering Force, Lok Sahayak Sena, and Para-Military Forces.
  • Family members (spouse/husband/wife and children, including adopted children) of persons who died while serving in Central Armed Forces are eligible for Ex-Servicemen reservation; however, age relaxation will not be provided to them.
  • Eligible cases for Ex-Servicemen reservation:
    • Retired voluntarily from such service after receiving pension; OR
    • Released from military service on medical grounds with medical and physical disability pension; OR

    • Released from service after completing specific service and receiving gratuity, after fulfilling period of service - including: persons retired from continuous service, persons with physical disability due to military service, and gazette prize winners.

Who Should NOT Apply for Bellary DCC Bank Recruitment 2026?

  • Candidates who do not meet the prescribed educational qualifications (degree for Manager/FDA; Second PUC for SDA; SSLC for Driver and Junior Servant) as on the last date of application.

  • Candidates below 18 years of age or above the maximum age limit applicable to their category.
  • OBC (Category-2A/2B/3A/3B) Creamy Layer candidates applying under reserved categories - only non-Creamy Layer OBC candidates are eligible for reservation.

  • Vehicle Driver candidates who do not hold a valid legal driving license.
  • Candidates currently employed in any organization who cannot produce an NOC from their employer.
  • Candidates who obtained degrees or certificates from institutions declared fake or derecognized by competent educational authorities - such applications will be rejected at any stage.
  • Candidates who provide false information or suppress facts - such candidates are liable for criminal prosecution and disqualification at any stage of the selection process.
  • Persons who are members of or active in any banned organization, or who have attempted to overthrow the Government of India, or who have been convicted under any law, or who have taken part in activities against the sovereignty or integrity of India, or who have been dismissed from any government service.
  • Candidates with mental illness or mental disability.
  • A male candidate who has more than one living wife, and a woman candidate who has married a man who already has another living wife, are not eligible.

  • Selecting the wrong category (General/SC/ST/OBC/EWS) - categories cannot be changed after submission; mismatched certificates lead to cancellation.

Selection Process: How Candidates Will Be Chosen

Selection for these IT Specialized Officer posts is interview-based, with no written examination stage. After the interview, shortlisted candidates go through a multi-step verification process before receiving a final appointment.

  1. Eligibility Screening – Applications are scrutinized against the post-specific eligibility criteria; only eligible candidates are shortlisted.
  2. Interview – Shortlisted candidates appear for a direct interview for the specific post they applied for.
  3. Preliminary Offer Letter – Issued to candidates who qualify in the interview.
  4. Verification Stage – Candidates undergo Background Verification, Police Verification, Medical Examination, and Documentation.
  5. Final Offer Letter – Issued once all verification steps are successfully completed.
  6. Probation Period – Selected candidates serve a 6-month probation, after which they are confirmed in their respective post.

The notification does not specify exact timelines between these stages; the interview date will be communicated directly to eligible candidates after screening.

Documents and Service Bond Requirements

Beyond the application form itself, candidates need to prepare supporting documents and understand the service commitment attached to this recruitment. This is an area where incomplete submissions commonly lead to rejection.

  • Self-attested photocopies of all relevant qualification and experience certificates must be enclosed with the application.
  • A domicile certificate of Maharashtra State is compulsory, since only Maharashtra residents are eligible to apply.
  • A recent passport-size photograph must be affixed (not pinned or stapled) to Annexure-1.
  • Selected candidates must execute an undertaking on ₹500 stamp paper committing to serve the Bank for a minimum of 5 years from the date of joining.
  • Breach of this undertaking requires payment of ₹10 lakh as liquidated damages upon demand, along with two surety bonds of ₹1 lakh each from two income-tax-paying sureties.
  • Candidates currently employed in government departments, PSUs, banks, or financial institutions must inform their employer in writing before applying and attach proof of this with the application.
  • At the time of joining, selected candidates must produce a proper discharge certificate from their previous employer.

  1. Visit the Bank's career page at https://msc.bank.in/career.
  2. Download Annexure-1 (Application Form) and Annexure-2 (Declaration Form).
  3. Fill in all details completely and affix a recent passport-size photograph.
  4. Attach self-attested photocopies of all relevant qualification and experience certificates.
  5. Superscribe the envelope as "Application for the post of [post name]."
  6. Send the sealed application via Post / Speed Post / Courier to:
    The Deputy General Manager (O.S.D.), HRD&M Department, The Maharashtra State Co-operative Bank Ltd., Sir Vithaldas Thackersey Smruti Bhavan, 9, Maharashtra Chamber of Commerce Lane, Fort, Mumbai – 400001, Post Box No. 472.
  7. Ensure the application physically reaches the Bank on or before 08.07.2026, up to 5:15 PM - postmark dates are not mentioned as sufficient.

Candidates can apply for only one post, so the post name should be decided before filling the form.

Special Eligibility Rules for Existing MSC Bank Employees

Current MSC Bank staff interested in these posts face a different set of conditions than external applicants, which is worth knowing before applying internally.

  • Applicants must first obtain written permission from the Bank, including prior approval of the Managing Director routed through their Department Incharge and the HRDM Manager.
  • Confirmed employees who meet all eligibility criteria can apply but are not entitled to any concession.
  • Official leave must be taken to attend the interview.
  • If selected in the immediate senior grade, salary is fixed as per prevailing practice based on regular service, excluding any Special Workload Allowance from the previous grade.
  • Employees applying for a post above their immediate seniority must resign from their current role after selection, following standard resignation rules.
  • Instead of the 5-year bond, internally selected employees execute an undertaking on ₹500 stamp paper to serve the Bank until retirement or superannuation.

Common Mistakes to Avoid When Applying

These are practical pitfalls based on how this recruitment is structured, meant to help candidates submit a clean application the first time.

  • Assuming this recruitment has an online portal - it is offline only, and any "apply online" claim for this advertisement should be treated with caution.
  • Forgetting to attach the Maharashtra domicile certificate, which is compulsory, not optional documentation.
  • Pinning or stapling the photograph on Annexure-1 instead of simply affixing it as instructed.
  • Applying for more than one post, since only single-post applications are accepted.
  • Sending unattested photocopies instead of self-attested ones.
  • Failing to inform a current government, PSU, or bank employer in writing before submitting the application.
  • Overlooking the one-year window to acquire a mandatory certification when it isn't already held.
  • Posting the application close to the deadline without accounting for postal transit time - the form must reach the Bank by 5:15 PM on 08.07.2026, not just be sent by that date.

This article explains the post-wise vacancy details, eligibility criteria, age limit, application fee, selection process and the complete online application procedure based strictly on the official notification.

PDC Bank Eligibility Criteria 2026

Eligibility for PDC Bank Recruitment 2026 is built on two pillars - educational qualification and relevant banking experience - and both vary by post. The details below help candidates check which post they qualify for before applying.

Educational Qualification

A graduate degree from a recognised university is the essential minimum requirement for every post in this recruitment; higher qualifications and professional certifications are preferred for managerial roles.

Manager / Deputy Manager / Executive / Senior Officer / Junior Officer Essential: Graduate in any subject from a recognised university. Post-graduation degree is desirable.

Candidates without a computer background must hold a Basic Computer Course certificate, or complete the relevant course within six months of joining the bank, to remain eligible for appointment.

Importantly, the notification specifies that all educational qualifications must be completed within the minimum course duration declared by the respective university or board. Candidates who took extra semesters or years to clear a backlog or ATKT are not eligible to apply for any of these posts.

PDC Bank Application Fee 2026

This section covers exactly how much candidates need to pay and how the fee should be submitted while applying for PDC Bank Recruitment 2026.

  • Application fee is ₹1000/- per post for all categories of candidates.
  • The fee must be paid online through UPI QR Code on the application portal.
  • The fee is non-refundable under any circumstances.
  • Candidates must save the fee payment confirmation/receipt for future reference.
  • Candidates applying for more than one post must pay the fee separately for each post applied to.

PDC Bank Selection Process 2026

Selection for all posts under PDC Bank Recruitment 2026 follows a two-stage process, with candidates applying to multiple posts required to clear a separate exam for each.

  • Written Examination for candidates who meet the eligibility criteria.
  • Interview for candidates shortlisted from the written examination.
  • Candidates applying for more than one post will be required to appear for a separate written examination for each post.
  • Final selection is based on combined performance in the written examination and interview, as per the bank's discretion.

PDC Bank Recruitment 2026: Competition Level Analysis

Competition for PDC Bank Recruitment 2026 will vary sharply by post, mainly due to the difference in vacancy count and the experience criteria attached to each role.

The Clerk post, with 100 vacancies and no prior experience requirement, is open to all fresh graduates meeting the 55% marks criterion and is expected to draw the highest volume of applications among all nine posts. The Junior Officer post, with 30 vacancies, also has a wide vacancy spread but is restricted to candidates with at least 3 years of relevant front-line banking experience, which narrows the applicant pool compared to Clerk. At the other end, posts such as General Manager (1 vacancy), Assistant General Manager (2), and Manager (2) demand 3 to 8+ years of managerial-level cooperative or commercial banking experience, which limits the eligible pool to seasoned banking professionals - even though the absolute number of applicants will be lower, competition per seat remains intense given how few vacancies are available at the senior level.

Who Should NOT Apply for PDC Bank Recruitment 2026

Based strictly on the eligibility conditions in the notification, candidates falling into the following categories should not apply, as their applications are likely to be rejected:

  • Candidates who do not meet the minimum or maximum age limit specified for the post as on 1 July 2026, particularly Clerk applicants outside the 20-30 year range, since no age relaxation applies to this post.
  • Candidates who completed their graduation or post-graduation by taking extra semesters or years beyond the minimum duration declared by their university/board to clear a backlog or ATKT - the notification explicitly excludes such candidates.
  • Candidates who do not hold the minimum years of relevant cooperative/commercial banking experience required for the specific post (for example, applying for Deputy General Manager without 5+ years of managerial experience).
  • Candidates who do not have, and cannot arrange, online payment facilities such as UPI, since only online fee payment is accepted.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

Many otherwise eligible candidates risk rejection or loss of the non-refundable fee due to avoidable errors. Keep these points in mind before submitting the application:

  • Sending a hard copy or offline application - the bank will accept only online applications for every post.
  • Not saving the UPI payment confirmation/receipt after paying the application fee, which the notification specifically asks candidates to retain.
  • Calculating age based on the application date instead of the official cut-off date of 1 July 2026.
  • Assuming one written exam covers multiple post applications - each post applied for requires a separate written examination.
  • For Clerk applicants from a non-computer background, forgetting to arrange the Basic Computer Course certificate within six months of joining.
  • Paying the non-refundable fee before carefully checking the age and experience criteria for the chosen post.

How to Apply for PDC Bank Recruitment 2026

The application process for PDC Bank Recruitment 2026 is entirely online. Follow these steps to submit your application correctly:

  1. Visit the official career portal at https://pdc.bank.in/career or the application portal at https://pdc.ugrowhrservices.com.
  2. Read the official notification carefully and identify the post(s) you are eligible for.
  3. Fill in the digital application form with accurate personal, educational and experience details.
  4. Upload all required documents as specified in the notification.
  5. Pay the application fee of ₹1000/- per post using the UPI QR Code provided on the portal.
  6. Save and download the fee payment confirmation for future reference.
  7. Submit the application before the deadline of 28 June 2026 and keep a copy/screenshot of the submitted form.

Apply Online for PDC Bank Recruitment 2026 through the official portal at https://pdc.ugrowhrservices.com, or visit https://pdc.bank.in/career for the career page.

Important Instructions for PDC Bank Recruitment 2026

Candidates should keep the following official conditions in mind before and after applying:

  • The probation period for all cadres is 1 year from the date of joining the bank, and may be extended if required.
  • All correspondence regarding examinations and interviews will be sent only through email - no other mode of communication will be used.
  • Candidates must bear their own travel and boarding expenses to attend the written examination and interview venue.
  • The bank reserves all rights related to the recruitment process without being required to give any reason.
  • The bank has an unrestricted right to extend the last date for submission of applications.

The Railway Recruitment Board has released the RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 on 22 June 2026, giving candidates their first look at where they'll sit for the second-stage exam on 2 July 2026. If you applied under CEN 05/2025 for Junior Engineer, Depot Material Superintendent, or Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant posts, you can now log in with your registration number and date of birth to check your allotted exam city, ahead of the admit card that follows on 28 June 2026.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

This guide walks you through the direct download link, the zone-wise login portals, exam shift timings, and exactly what the slip does (and doesn't) tell you so you can start planning your travel right away.

What Is the RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026?

Before downloading anything, it helps to know exactly what this document is and isn't. Here's the short answer: it's an advance notice of your exam city, not your entry ticket to the exam hall.

The city intimation slip is a preliminary notice issued by RRB purely to tell candidates which city their CBT 2 exam centre will fall in. It does not carry the exact venue address, reporting time, or entry instructions those details arrive only with the admit card. The slip exists so candidates have enough lead time to book trains, buses, or accommodation if their allotted city is far from home, rather than scrambling once the admit card lands just days before the exam.

RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 - Key Details at a Glance

City Intimation Slip Release Date 22 June 2026
CBT 2 Admit Card Release Date 28 June 2026
CBT 2 Exam Date 2 July 2026
Number of Shifts 3
Login Credentials Required Registration Number + Date of Birth/Password
Official Website rrbcdg.gov.in (and respective zonal RRB sites)

RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 Direct Download Link

The Railway Recruitment Board activated the city intimation login link on its official regional portals on 22 June 2026. Candidates need to click through to the login page, enter their registration number and date of birth, and the system will display the allotted exam city on screen.

Direct Link: RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026

Keep in mind that the city slip itself is not downloadable as a print-ready hall ticket the way an admit card is it simply displays your allotted city, state, exam date, and shift on screen after login. Note this down or take a screenshot for your own reference.

How to Check the RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 (Step-by-Step)

If this is your first time accessing the city slip, follow these steps exactly to avoid login errors.

The process is identical across all RRB zones, though each zone uses its own regional website. Here's the complete sequence:

  1. Visit the official website of the RRB zone you applied under (see the zone-wise list below).
  2. On the homepage, look under the "Latest News" or "Notice Board" section for the link reading "CEN 05/2025 RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026."
  3. Click the link you'll be redirected to a login page.
  4. Enter your Registration Number (the unique ID sent to your email/mobile after form submission) and your Date of Birth in DDMMYYYY format as the password.
  5. Enter the CAPTCHA code shown on screen.
  6. Click Submit/Login to view your allotted exam city, state, date, and shift.
  7. Note down or screenshot the details for your own records, since this isn't a printable document like the admit card.

What Information Does the RRB JE City Slip Actually Contain?

Knowing what's printed on the slip helps you double-check your own details for accuracy the moment you log in.

The city intimation slip is intentionally limited to preliminary identification and location details nothing related to the exact venue. Specifically, it shows:

  • Candidate's full name
  • Registration number
  • Post applied for (JE/DMS/CMA)
  • Allotted exam city and state
  • Scheduled exam date
  • Assigned shift number

What it does not include: the exact exam centre name, full address, reporting time, or gate closure time. Those appear only on the admit card.

RRB JE CBT 2 Exam Shift Timings 2026

Since the CBT 2 exam runs across three shifts in a single day, knowing your assigned slot matters for planning your morning (or afternoon, or evening).

The exam is conducted as a 120-minute computer-based test, split into three shifts to accommodate the large candidate pool appearing under CEN 05/2025. Reporting and gate closure times are strict, so candidates should plan to arrive well ahead of the listed closure time.

Shift Reporting Time Gate Closure Time Exam Start Time
Shift 1 7:30 AM 8:30 AM 9:00 AM
Shift 2 11:15 AM 12:15 PM 12:45 PM
Shift 3 3:00 PM 4:00 PM 4:30 PM

Your exact shift assignment will be confirmed on both the city intimation slip and, later, the admit card always go by what's printed on your own document rather than assuming a shift based on this table.

RRB JE City Intimation Slip vs Admit Card: What's the Difference?

A lot of candidates confuse the two, so here's a direct comparison to clear that up.

The city slip and the admit card serve entirely different purposes, even though both relate to the same exam. The city slip is informational only; the admit card is your mandatory entry document.

Typical Release Window ~10 days before exam ~4 days before exam
Venue Detail City and state only Full centre name and address
Valid for Exam Entry No Yes, mandatory

RRB JE CBT 2 Admit Card 2026: What Comes Next

Once you've checked your city, the next document to watch for is the admit card the one you'll actually need on exam day.

The RRB JE CBT 2 Admit Card 2026 will be released on 28 June 2026, four days ahead of the 2 July exam. Unlike the city slip, the admit card carries the complete exam centre address, your final reporting time, gate closure time, and exam-day instructions. It must be downloaded, printed, and carried to the centre along with a valid photo ID entry will not be permitted without it.

To download the admit card when it goes live:

RRB Group D Result 2026 - Latest Update

This section explains the most recent development in the RRB Group D result timeline, including the court case status and the revised expected release date.

The Telangana High Court has disposed of the petition concerning Course Completed Act Apprentice (CCAA) weightage marks on 16th June 2026, removing the stay that had earlier delayed the result. With the legal hurdle cleared, the Railway Recruitment Board is now expected to declare the RRB Group D Result 2026 in the 4th week of June 2026, along with the scorecard, merit list, and cut off marks. As a precautionary step, the court has directed RRB to keep 15 vacancies reserved until final disposal of the main writ petition, while the remaining 32,423 posts will be filled through the regular recruitment process. RRB has also opened an application modification window for CCAA candidates from 17th June to 23rd June 2026, allowing them to update NCVT certificate details and marks before the result is finalised.

RRB Group D Result 2026 Overview
